536	### HE-F7 Mark ring eviction, lifetime and ageing
537	
538	The mark ring eviction, lifetime and ageing formula is defined as:
539	
540	`insert of kind K at its quota evicts argmin(mark_id) over kind = K;   insert of a SMEAR into a full ring evicts argmin(mark_id) over kind = SMEAR;   n_other_max = MARK_QUOTA_RIME + MARK_QUOTA_HAIRLINES + MARK_QUOTA_STRUCK;   life_left ← life_left − HORROR_RUN_TICKS per run while the mark's section is loaded, removed at life_left ≤ 0;   stage = min(2, floor(3 × (MARK_LIFE_TICKS − life_left) / MARK_LIFE_TICKS));   smear_retention_ticks = (MAX_MARKS − n_other_max) × MARK_SPACING_PX × 1000 / V_CREEP_MPX;   MARK_LIFE_TICKS ≥ smear_retention_ticks ≥ TRAIL_TARGET_TICKS;   MAX_MARKS − n_other_max ≥ ceil(TRAIL_TARGET_TICKS × V_CREEP_MPX / (MARK_SPACING_PX × 1000))` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
541	
542	**Variables:**
543	
544	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
545	|---|---|---|---|---|
546	| `mark_id` | int | ≥ 1, never reused | block counter | Insertion order |
547	| `kind` | enum | SMEAR, RIME, HAIRLINES, STRUCK | block | Mark kind (HE-27) |
548	| `MAX_MARKS` | int | `n_other_max + 19`..48 (32..48 at the placeholders), [PH] 32 | Horror | Ring size. Raised from 24 to 32 in the design review (at 24 the smear history was `(24 − 9) × 96 = 1440` ticks, below the 1800 target); the range's floor now follows the quotas, so the range no longer contradicts its own relation *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; a registry request |
549	| `MARK_LIFE_TICKS` | int ticks | `smear_retention_ticks`..54000 (1824 is the derived floor at the placeholders; 3600 is the lowest authored value), [PH] 18000 | Horror | Lifetime of a mark in a loaded section; the lower bound is asserted at load *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
550	| `MARK_SPACING_PX` | int px | 48..144, [PH] 96 | Horror | One SMEAR per this much travel (two tiles); plus one touch-down SMEAR per REACH start |
551	| `CHILL_SPACING_PX` | int px | 192..768, [PH] 384 | Horror | One CHILL deposit and rime mark per this much travel, and at each LURK dwell start |
552	| `n_other_max` | int | DERIVED 13 | the three quotas | `MARK_QUOTA_RIME` 7 + `MARK_QUOTA_HAIRLINES` 3 + `MARK_QUOTA_STRUCK` 3. The rime quota is `ceil(MAX_MARKS / (CHILL_SPACING_PX / MARK_SPACING_PX + 1))` = `ceil(32 / 5)` = 7 (one rime per five ring slots of creep); the other two follow the three-strike ladder. Asserted at data load as arithmetic (`n_other_max + 19 <= MAX_MARKS`), never as a runtime-derived fixture *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
553	| `MARK_QUOTA_RIME` / `MARK_QUOTA_HAIRLINES` / `MARK_QUOTA_STRUCK` | int | 1..12 / 1..6 / 1..6, [PH] 7 / 3 / 3, and `sum + 19 <= MAX_MARKS` | Horror | Per-kind ring quotas (HE-30); an insert at quota evicts the oldest of its own kind *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
554	| `TRAIL_TARGET_TICKS` | int ticks | 1800..3600, [PH] 1800 | game-designer target (the hidden-entity investigation window), not a runtime value | The trail an investigator arriving up to 30 s late should still find |
555	| `V_CREEP_MPX` | int | 1000 | HE-F6 | Creep speed |
556	| `MARKS_PER_RUN_MAX` | int | 1..4, [PH] 2 | Horror | Inserts per run; over the cap, priority STRUCK, then HAIRLINES, then RIME, then SMEAR; a dropped insert is counted `horror_marks_withheld` |
557	
558	**Output Range:** `stage` in {0, 1, 2}: exactly three frame stages for smear and rime (and two for hairlines), so physical age is readable without a meter (Pillar 1) and no continuous value is drawn. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* `smear_retention_ticks` is now a **guaranteed minimum**, because the quotas fix `n_other_max` at 13: at the placeholders `(32 − 13) × 96 × 1000 / 1000 = 1824` ticks at creep speed, at or above `TRAIL_TARGET_TICKS` 1800 whatever the history (an 18000-tick CALM LURK fills the rime quota and no more; a 3600-tick breach fills the HAIRLINES and STRUCK quotas and no more, the oldest of a kind being replaced); more smear history, up to 2112 ticks with only ten others resident, is available but not guaranteed. At `V_HUNT_MPX` the same ring holds `19 × 96 × 1000 / 1500 = 1216` ticks, below the target: the BREACH approach trail is short-lived by construction (the horror covers distance faster than a smear can age), the hidden-entity investigation window is defined on the creep trail, and the shortfall is accepted and logged (Open Question 20). The touch-down SMEAR of each REACH is a SMEAR and competes with the travel smears, but REACHes occur only in BREACH, where that shortfall is already accepted. The ring, not the lifetime, is the binding bound on a creeping horror; the lifetime exists so a frozen loaded body does not keep stale marks forever.
559	
560	**Example:** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* the ring is full at 32 with 3 hairline marks, 3 STRUCK marks, 7 rime marks and 19 smears. A new smear evicts the oldest smear and never a hairline; a fourth HAIRLINES mark evicts the oldest HAIRLINES mark and nothing else; an eighth rime evicts the oldest rime. There is always a smear to evict because `32 > 13`. The relation `MAX_MARKS − n_other_max >= ceil(TRAIL_TARGET_TICKS × V_CREEP_MPX / (MARK_SPACING_PX × 1000))` = 19 is an arithmetic assertion the data load makes: `13 + 19 = 32` passes, and a quota set summing to 14 with `MAX_MARKS` 32 fails the load. Ageing: a mark with `life_left` 12000 has age 6000 and `stage = floor(3 × 6000 / 18000) = 1`; at `life_left` 5999 the age is 12001 and the stage is 2.
561	
562	**Registry candidate:** `mark_ring_retention`.

564	### HE-F8 Target selection from `lux_pm`
565	
566	The target selection formula is defined as:
567	
568	`candidates = { s : living(s) ∧ ¬DOWNED(s) ∧ ¬IN_POD(s) ∧ actor_section(s) ∈ body_scope ∧ lit(s) };   target = argmax over candidates of (lux_pm(s), −seat_id);   candidates = ∅ ⇒ target = ANCHOR (HE-16 (3))`
569	
570	`body_scope` is `locus_body` in TELL, BREACH and SUBSIDING and the record's own body in CALM. Nothing is stored between runs.
571	
572	**Variables:**
573	
574	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
575	|---|---|---|---|---|
576	| `lux_pm(s)` | int permille | 0..1000 | Emitter `lux(ref)` | The seat's illumination; the owner stands in their own light (EM-21), so a seat with its lamp on reads 1000 |
577	| `lit(s)` | bool | — | derived here: `lux_pm(s) >= LIT_ON_PM` (150, CITED) | Stateless, recomputed every run, nothing stored. **Not the Emitter's `lit` bit** (a hysteresis on `act_lux_pm`, which excludes the owner's own beam and the BEACON; a lone lamp-on player reads `act_lux_pm` 0) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
578	| `seat_id` | int | ≥ 0 | Body | Tie-break: lowest wins |
579	| `ANCHOR` | position | Layout `anchor_geometry` | HE-16 (3) | The target when no candidate is lit |
580	
581	**Output Range:** a seat id or ANCHOR; one `lux(ref)` read per candidate per run, zero probes (HE-43).
582	
583	**Example:** seat A `lux_pm` 1000 (lamp on), seat B 0 (dark): target A. Seat A switches the lamp off: no lit candidate, target ANCHOR on the next run, and nothing remembers A (the target is not persisted). A thrown Chemlight pool reads 700 only for a seat that stands in it; the horror targets whichever *seat* is lit, never the pool (a pool is not a seat, HE-13). Two lit seats at 1000 and 1000: the lower `seat_id` wins; a stateless argmax can alternate as lamps change (C-HE-19, Vertical Slice). *Further cases (design review):* a seat with its lamp off under a lit fixture reading 400 is lit (`400 >= 150`) and is the target while a dark seat is not; a seat with its lamp off whose only light is the BEACON's sweep is lit only on the runs where `lux_pm >= 150` (it counts in `lux_pm`, not in `act_lux_pm`) and the next run's target may differ, but a REACH already begun keeps its locked P; a seat with its lamp on standing in a 400 fixture pool and a seat with its lamp off in a 700 Chemlight pool: the lamp-on seat reads 1000 and wins, so the argmax is the lamp, not the amount *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
584	
585	**Registry candidate:** `horror_target_rule`.

587	### HE-F9 Ingress timing and entry choice
588	
589	The ingress timing and entry choice formula is defined as:
590	
591	`transit_until_T = tell_enter_T + INGRESS_DELAY_TICKS;   fallback_T = transit_until_T + STALK_VISIBLE_FLOOR_TICKS;   arrive_T = min{ T ≥ transit_until_T : T mod 5 = 0 ∧ ( legal_entry(T) ∨ (T ≥ fallback_T + INGRESS_MARK_LEAD_TICKS ∧ fallback_entry(T)) ) };   stalk_visible_min = TELL_MIN_TICKS − INGRESS_DELAY_TICKS;   D_entry_max = LURK_STANDOFF_PX + floor(stalk_visible_min × V_CREEP_MPX / 1000);   INGRESS_DELAY_TICKS + STALK_VISIBLE_FLOOR_TICKS + INGRESS_MARK_LEAD_TICKS ≤ TELL_MIN_TICKS` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
592	
593	`legal_entry(T)` selects, among the hull entries of `locus_body` at room-hop distance 1 from the room of the highest-`lux_pm` living seat (none lit or present: the locus section's outermost compartment), a hull segment whose room holds no living seat and which lies at least `LURK_STANDOFF_PX` from every living seat **that is `linked` to it (HE-19)**; ties lowest hop, then lowest room id, then lowest hull-segment id. A *hull entry* is an `anchor_geometry` point of a hull-bearing compartment that lies within `HULL_CONTACT_PX` of a hull face, paired with the lowest id returned by `hull_segments_near(section_id, anchor_px, HULL_CONTACT_PX)`; there is no `solid_in` sampling and no unpublished room-to-segment read. 634	### HE-F11 L3 disturbance strength and duration bound
635	
636	The L3 disturbance strength and duration formula is defined as:
637	
638	`S_hi = 1000 − MOD_FLOOR_PM;   strength_pm = L3_STRENGTH_LO_PM + (h2 mod (S_hi − L3_STRENGTH_LO_PM + 1));   dur_ticks = L3_DUR_LO + (h3 mod (L3_DUR_HI − L3_DUR_LO + 1));   start iff h1 mod 1000 < L3_START_PM ∧ T ≥ last_end_T + L3_MIN_GAP_TICKS;   L3_STRENGTH_LO_PM ≤ S_hi`
639	
640	`h1`, `h2`, `h3` are `he_hash(emitter_id, run_n, 0, SALT_L3_START)`, `…SALT_L3_STRENGTH)` and `…SALT_L3_DUR)` (HE-42: non-negative, golden vectors in AC-HE-139), never `rng_derive`. The result enters Lighting's registered `modifier_stack` as the L3 factor, whose floor `MOD_FLOOR_PM` already clamps the chain; Horror never restates or applies that clamp. **Sign convention** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: `strength_pm` is a dip **depth**, like Lighting's `DIP_DEPTH_PM` (`M1 = 1000 − DIP_DEPTH_PM` during a dip, LO D.15); Lighting's L3 factor is `M3 = 1000 − strength_pm` (1000 = no dip). **Worked LO-18 example:** `strength_pm` 374 gives `M3 = 626`; with a concurrent gutter `M1 = 700`, an idle tell `M2 = 1000` and `MOD_FLOOR_PM` 600, `m_mod = clamp(floor(700 × 1000 × 626 / 10^6), 600, 1000) = clamp(438, 600, 1000) = 600` (the floor binds); with `M1 = 1000` the same dip is `clamp(626, 600, 1000) = 626`. The reduced-motion cap is stated in Tuning Knobs (`L3_STRENGTH_RM_CAP_PM`).
641	
642	**Variables:**
643	
644	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
645	|---|---|---|---|---|
646	| `MOD_FLOOR_PM` | int permille | 600, range 400..800 [PH] (CITED) | 2D Lighting & Occlusion, registry | The deepest any modifier chain may dim a lamp |
647	| `S_hi` | int permille | DERIVED (400 at the placeholder; the formula is cited, never the bare number) | this formula | Strength ceiling |
648	| `L3_STRENGTH_LO_PM` ★ | int permille | 50..`S_hi`, [PH] 150 | Horror | Shallowest dip (a depth: `M3 = 1000 − strength_pm`) |

760	The stationary-seat lethality formula is defined as:
761	
762	`s_1 = t_arrive;   s_{k+1} = s_k + U_k + STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS + t_back;   T_3 = t_arrive + U_1 + U_2 + U_3 + 2 × (STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS + t_back);   T_2 = t_arrive + U_1 + U_2 + (STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS + t_back);   third REACH starts inside a breach of length B iff s_3 < B;   P_3(λ) = 1 − e^{−λ} × (1 + λ + λ²/2) (fresh suit, I_0 ≥ 8900: three landed strikes kill);   P_2(λ) = 1 − e^{−λ} × (1 + λ) (worn or patched suit, I_0 < 8900: two kill);   λ = E_s × n × p` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
763	
764	The first four terms are integer simulation arithmetic; `P_death` is design analysis (real arithmetic, never hashed): the probability of at least three landed strikes (fresh suit) or two (worn or patched suit) in a session when strikes arrive as a Poisson process (no passive integrity regeneration exists, so hits accumulate until `patch_integrity`, HE-F3). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* The fresh-suit tail alone understated lethality and was only a lower bound; `k_fail(I) = 3` needs `I >= 8900` (`floor((I − 2500) / 3200) + 1`), so every patched suit (cap at most 6900) and every suit after one landed strike (6800) is in the two-strike state.
765	
766	**Variables:**
767	
768	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
769	|---|---|---|---|---|
770	| `U_k` | int ticks | 95..180 (18 values) | HE-F5 | The k-th telegraph length |
771	| `t_arrive`, `t_back` | int ticks | `t_arrive` 0..70 (65 at the pinned fixture, HE-F13); `t_back` 65 | HE-F13, HE-F15 | First approach and per-cycle return; the figures below use the pinned `t_arrive` 65 unless a range is named *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
772	| `B` | int ticks | `BREACH_MIN_TICKS` 900 .. `BREACH_MAX_TICKS` 3600 (CITED) | Attention, registry | BREACH length; a REACH may begin only while the phase is BREACH and then resolves into SUBSIDING if the predicate holds (HE-17) |
773	| `E_s` | real | 3..8 *(provisional — Attention's breaches per session is undesigned as a rate)* | Attention | Told breaches per session with the seat in the locus body |
774	| `n` | real | 0..8 | HE-F15 | REACH attempts that reach the seat per breach (a stationary seat sees 7 or 8 starts in a 3600-tick breach, so 8 is the ceiling) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
775	| `p` | real | 0..1 | playtest | Per-attempt probability that the seat is struck (inattention, late reaction, cornered, carrying); **this is the lethality dial** |
776	| `λ` | real | ≥ 0 | derived | Expected landed strikes per session |
777	
778	**Output Range:** `T_3` in 1080..1335 ticks after BREACH entry (18.0 to 22.3 s), mean 1207.5 (20.1 s). The earliest possible third REACH start is `s_3 = 65 + 95 + 95 + 730 = 985`, so a stationary seat **with a fresh suit (`I_0 >= 8900`, three strikes needed) cannot be killed in a minimum-length breach** (`B = 900`: two starts, rung CRITICAL, stagger, a seat that then moves lives); it can in any breach of at least 986 ticks and certainly (probability 1) in any breach of at least 1156 ticks. REACH starts for a stationary seat: 2 at `B = 900`, 4 at `B = 1800`, 7 or 8 at `B = 3600`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **The claim is conditioned on `I_0`:** with `t_arrive` 0 the earliest third REACH start is `s_3 = 0 + 95 + 95 + 730 = 920`, still after 900, and `T_3` runs 1015..1270 at `t_arrive` 0 and 1085..1340 at 70 (1080..1335 at the pinned 65); but a **worn or patched suit that stands still is killed in a minimum-length breach with probability 1**: `T_2` is 620 to 790 ticks after BREACH entry at the pinned fixture (555..725 at `t_arrive` 0), and the second REACH starts at `s_2 = t_arrive + U_1 + 365` = 525..610, always before 900, so all 324 draw pairs end in FAILED (DOWNED then the Controller's clock). The 6800 row (one landed strike already) is therefore the same state as a patched suit: two further strikes kill. *Scope note (design review 2026-10-27):* the model needs no compound term for a RUPTURE on a struck seat, because HE-16 (2) forbids a RUPTURE on a strike that hits a seat (E-HE-56); and the figures here are stated at `UNFOLD_SCALE_PCT` 100, a larger scale stretches every `U_k` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
779	
780	**Example:** `P(s_3 < B)` over the 18 × 18 equiprobable draw pairs: 0 at 900, 0.3 % at 990, 1.9 % at 1000, 28.1 % at 1050, 75.9 % at 1100, 99.7 % at 1155, 100 % at 1156. Session ratchet: `λ = 0.5` gives 1.4 %, `λ = 1.0` gives 8.0 % (the median target), `λ = 1.5` gives 19.1 %, `λ = 2.4` gives 43.0 %, `λ = 3.0` gives 57.7 %, `λ = 6.0` gives 93.8 %. With `E_s = 4` and `n = 6`, `p = 5 %` gives `λ = 1.2` and about 12 %; `p = 10 %` gives `λ = 2.4` and 43 % (fresh suit). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **Worn or patched suit** (`P_2`): `λ = 0.5` gives 9.0 %, `λ = 1.0` gives 26.4 %, `λ = 1.5` gives 44.2 %, `λ = 2.4` gives 69.2 %, `λ = 3.0` gives 80.1 %, `λ = 6.0` gives 98.3 %; `p = 5 %` (`λ = 1.2`) gives about 33.7 % where the fresh suit gives 12 %. The session ratchet is steeper than the fresh-suit table alone suggests, which is why `patch_integrity` availability (Suit's) is one of the named lethality dials. The whole "death is a bitch" dial is the per-attempt miss rate `p`, set by telegraph legibility (HE-14), not by any number in the knob table.
781	
782	**Registry candidate:** `stationary_seat_lethality` (the integer part only).
783	
784	### HE-F17 Hull act ladder gate
785	
786	The hull act ladder formula is defined as:
787	
788	`rupture_ok = (seg ∈ gouged_seg_ids) ∧ ruptures_epoch < RUPTURES_PER_EPOCH_MAX ∧ exogenous_permitted(section(seg)) ∧ hit_list = ∅;   gouge_ok = gouges_epoch < GOUGES_PER_EPOCH_MAX ∧ exogenous_permitted(section(seg));   deposit(STRIKE at P within HULL_CONTACT_PX of seg) = RUPTURE if rupture_ok, else GOUGE if gouge_ok, else none;   on a GOUGE: gouged_seg_ids ← gouged_seg_ids ∪ {seg} (after the test above);   lint: STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS < min_gap = STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS + UNFOLD_LO` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
789	
790	One hull deposit kind per STRIKE: the RUPTURE act is a later act than the GOUGE act it requires (HE-16 (2); *orchestrator ruling: HE-16 is silent on a strike where both are eligible, and one deposit per act keeps each act preceded by its own REACH*). The anchor REACH (no lit seat) may deposit one GOUGE only (`ANCHOR_REACH_GOUGES` 1), never RUPTURE. The kind is hull only (lint `GOUGE_NON_HULL`).
791	
792	**Variables:**
793	
794	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
795	|---|---|---|---|---|
796	| `gouges_epoch`, `ruptures_epoch` | int | 0..`GOUGES_PER_EPOCH_MAX`, 0..`RUPTURES_PER_EPOCH_MAX` | block (reset lazily at the first run that sees a new `tell_epoch`, transition guard 2) | Hull acts this `tell_epoch` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
797	| `GOUGES_PER_EPOCH_MAX` | int | 0..6, [PH] 3 | Horror | Hull GOUGE ceiling per epoch |
798	| `RUPTURES_PER_EPOCH_MAX` | int | 0..1, [PH] 1 | Horror | A RUPTURE needs a Graph-told clock afterwards (decompression, `RUPTURE_HP` 3600, registry, LSG:102) |
799	| `HULL_CONTACT_PX` | int px | 12..48, [PH] 24 | Horror | P within this of a hull-segment face |
800	| `gouged_seg_ids` | ascending int list | length at most `GOUGES_PER_EPOCH_MAX` and at most `gouges_epoch` | block (emptied by guard 2) | The hull-segment ids this epoch's GOUGEs landed on: the whole gouge ledger the RUPTURE gate reads (ids only, no time) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
801	| `magnitude` | int bp | ≤ `FOOTPRINT_MAX_GOUGE_BP` 2500 (registry, LSG:914, CITED) | Graph | M17 magnitude |
802	
803	**Output Range:** per epoch at most 3 GOUGE and 1 RUPTURE, hence at most 4 hull-deposit M17 calls from strikes (plus the anchor GOUGE, which counts against `GOUGES_PER_EPOCH_MAX`). The earlier time clause `T ≥ gouge_T + STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS` is **deleted** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: consecutive strikes are at least `min_gap` = `STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS + UNFOLD_LO` = 395 apart (HE-F15), which exceeds `STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS` for any `UNFOLD_LO >= 1`, so the clause could never decide an outcome and a stored time would only add restore state. The ordering that matters, a GOUGE strictly earlier than the RUPTURE that needs it and never in the same strike (it forbids a same-act GOUGE-plus-RUPTURE and keeps the scrape ahead of the tear), is carried by membership in `gouged_seg_ids` tested before the append; the lint in the formula guards the one assumption it rests on.
804	
805	**Example:** a lit seat stands beside a hull face. Strike one at `T = 1075`: P within 24 px of segment S, no GOUGE yet: `deposit = GOUGE` (`gouges_epoch = 1`, S appended to `gouged_seg_ids`), radial hairlines laid. Strike two at `T = 1550` on S, the seat having walked out of the disc (`hit_list = ∅`): `rupture_ok` (S ∈ `gouged_seg_ids`, `ruptures_epoch 0 < 1`, nobody in the disc): `deposit = RUPTURE`; had the seat stood still and been struck, `rupture_ok` is false and the deposit is `GOUGE` (if under 3) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Strike three on S: `ruptures_epoch = 1`, so `GOUGE` (if under 3). A GOUGE sets the segment `fatigued`, an ENDOGENOUS creep that outlives the breach and sits under the Graph's own `W_MIN_WARNING_S` gate (HE-16 (4)); Horror neither alters nor shortens it.
806	
807	**Registry candidate:** `hull_act_ladder`.
808	
809	### HE-F18 Presentation interpolation alpha (render side only)
810	
811	The presentation interpolation alpha formula is defined as:
812	
813	`alpha5 = ((T_now − T_run) + tick_alpha) / HORROR_RUN_TICKS;   draw_pos = pos_prev + (pos_curr − pos_prev) × alpha5`
814	
815	This is presentation arithmetic (real numbers, never hashed, never in a SIM block); the rig *pose* is stepped once per run and never tweened (PIPE row 14). It is owed to the Pipeline because the kernel's `tick_alpha` spans one tick, not five (C-HE-14).
816	
817	**Variables:**
818	
819	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
820	|---|---|---|---|---|
821	| `T_now`, `T_run` | int tick | — | Kernel | The presented tick and the tick of the most recent Horror run |
822	| `tick_alpha` | real | [0, 1] | Kernel | Fraction within the current tick |
823	| `pos_prev`, `pos_curr` | int px | — | `horror.view` | Positions at the previous and the latest run |
824	
825	**Output Range:** `alpha5` in [0, 1]. **Example:** two ticks after the run with `tick_alpha` 0.5: `alpha5 = (2 + 0.5) / 5 = 0.5`, the draw position is the midpoint. A rig pose change on any tick that is not a multiple of 5 fails the cadence criterion.
826	
827	**Registry candidate:** none (render-side; owed to the Pipeline).
828

128	## Detailed Design
129	
130	### Core Rules
131	
132	Rule ids are `HE-n`; formulas `HE-F n` (Formulas section, ids reserved in the index at the end of this section); edge cases `E-HE-n`; acceptance criteria `AC-HE-n`; conflicts `C-HE-n`. Every Horror-owned number is `[PLACEHOLDER]` and a registry candidate unless marked CITED (a locked name quoted verbatim with its registry value) or DERIVED. The Graph's `RUPTURE_HP`, `BREACH_HP`, `FOOTPRINT_MAX_Q`, `FOOTPRINT_MAX_GOUGE_BP`, `STRESS_HOLD_STEPS` and `C_TILE` are Life-Support Graph registry constants (registered 2026-10-27), cited with the registry value and their LSG line and never restated as Horror's own. Rules state observable behaviour and contracts; implementation patterns are marked "-> ADR candidate". "Run" means one execution of the `horror.step` hook (every 5th tick).
133	
134	#### Group A — Identity, scope and ownership
135	
136	**HE-1. One type, one instance, one behaviour cycle.** *Rule.* MVP ships exactly one type row, `horror_t01` (a placeholder name, renamed never aliased: floor-attached, three-branch, about 1.5 times crewmate height, one extensible reach limb; the art bible's outer-ring working target, ART:546), at most `HORROR_MAX_MVP` 1 resident record, and one behaviour cycle: **LURK (CALM) / STALK (TELL) → REACH (telegraph) → STRIKE → RETREAT**, plus `TRANSIT` while it passes through a hull. The motion vocabulary of the art matrix maps onto it as *creep* (LURK, STALK, RETREAT), *unfold* (REACH) and *snap* (STRIKE). "One behaviour" is **one cycle of one type, never three monsters.** More types, per-ring rosters, filament-riders, hidden-entity wiring, `repel`, flares and decoys, and co-op replication are Vertical Slice and are named in Open Questions and in the block shape only. *Why.* The concept's MVP item 4 is "Attention with one threshold and one horror behaviour"; AT-11 makes a told breach without teeth a named design failure (cry-wolf; commit dominates abort), and the art bible names the reach as the signature image (ART 5.4). *Cites.* AT:197, AT:373, CON MVP definition, ART:546.
137	
138	**HE-2. A real horror is a true SIM entity that touches nothing optical.** *Rule.* A horror has a true integer position in its own block, is solid to Layout solids and to nothing else (it passes through crewmates and they through it, BDY-17), is drawn in the single Y-sorted layer so its sprite hides what stands behind it, is hidden by walls and by darkness, and is revealed only by light. It **contributes no occluder, casts no shadow, emits nothing, and never changes the beam, any subject's `lux`, `lit` or any emitter field.** "Real occlusion" in the index row and the routed thread is read as *visual opacity by draw order plus locomotion against Layout solids*, never as a `LightOccluder2D`. Nothing a horror does is a light event except the disturbance state of HE-35, which Lighting reads and executes. *Why.* Three designed GDDs decide it (EM-20 (c) and AC-24; Lighting rail 10 "Horrors cast no shadow and emit nothing" and AC-LO-16; Failure & Trail FT-31) and the art bible's own recommendation agrees (ART:296); a horror shadow would destroy the free stage-2 sanity falsifier "a shadow with no occluder" and with it Pillar 4's "no lie is unfalsifiable". "Displace dust" from the art bible is retained in spirit through the marks of HE-30, not through the Attention Presenter's shared dust process. *(orchestrator ruling: option A, affirmed by the creative-director at the CD-GDD-ALIGN gate as R1; the fiction gloss "the web does not stop light; it only takes it" is adopted; the wording refreshes are owed rows, never edits here.)* **Gate.** Until the owed ART:542, ART 5.5, PIPE:140 and IDX:35 refresh rows land, the art bible and this GDD contradict each other; those rows are a BLOCKING precondition of `/asset-spec` for the rig (AC-HE-123), as C-HE-21 is for rime. *Cites.* EM:208, LO:151, FT:199, ART:296, ART:542.
139	
140	**HE-3. Block and hook identity.** *Rule.* Block `horror.state`: class `SIM`, `persist` true, `persist_scope` WORLD, scope SHARED, `repl_hint` SHARED_SUMMARY, `schema_version` 1, `supported_versions` [1], `restore_after` `[layout.state, graph.state, emitter.state, attention.state]`. Hook `horror.step`: divisor 5, offset 0, `after: [attention.step, emitter.place]` (the must-repeats of Attention (AT:373), the Emitter (EM AC-60) and the kernel (KRN:201), exactly as ruled; C-HE-20 closed). A hook id that is unknown at boot fails boot (CR-3, no alias concept); grep of `horror.step`, `horror.state` and `horror.view` across the neighbours before closing found no collision. The read view is `horror.view` (HE-37). *Why.* `body.integrate` precedes `horror.step` on every Horror tick through `emitter.place`'s own `after` list (EM:104: `after: [body.integrate, graph.propagate.failure]`) and the CR-3 total order, so the same-tick seat read that the exact walk-out arithmetic of HE-F2 needs holds without extending the ruled list; Horror writes nothing Body reads, so no cycle can form. A one-tick-stale seat read would let an escaping seat read up to 2 px closer than it is. *Cites.* KRN:71, KRN:201, EM:104, AT:125-131, BDY-8.
141	
142	**HE-4. Cadence: one run is one rig pose, and what Horror reads between Attention's runs.** *Rule.* `horror.step` runs on ticks that are multiples of 5 (12 Hz), so one run is exactly one 12 fps rig pose (PIPE row 14). Attention and the Graph run at divisor 6; LCM(5, 6) = 30, so the two hooks coincide only when `T mod 30 = 0`, and CR-3's `after` orders the pair only on those ticks. On every other run Horror reads `attention.view` **as committed by Attention's most recent run**; this is a reading of committed state, not a new kernel rule. Presentation interpolates `pos_prev` to `pos_curr` across the five ticks of a run; the rig pose is stepped, never tweened. Every Horror duration is authored as an integer count of runs and published in ticks as `runs × 5` (`HORROR_RUN_TICKS` 5, DERIVED from the divisor); a duration that is not a multiple of 5 is a data-load lint failure (it would silently round up to the next run, a 1 to 4 tick bias that matters at the `UNFOLD_LO` bound). **The lint covers every SIM-clock duration** (`UNFOLD_LO`, `UNFOLD_HI`, `STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS`, `INGRESS_DELAY_TICKS`, `RETURN_DELAY_TICKS`, `LURK_DWELL_TICKS` and the rest of the type row); it **exempts the L3 disturbance lengths `L3_DUR_LO` and `L3_DUR_HI`** (18 and 30), which are published to Lighting in ticks and are presentation-timed (LO-19, the gutter grammar), not run-quantised: a disturbance *starts* on a run, its length does not round to one (C-HE-29). *Cites.* PIPE:303, KRN:71, HE-F5.
143	
144	**HE-5. Data-driven type row.** *Rule.* Every per-type value lives in a data file keyed by `type_id`; behaviour code is generic over the row and contains no behavioural constant. A row carries: `v_creep_mpx`, `v_hunt_mpx`, `r_snap_px`, `reach_range_px`, `hull_contact_px`, `strike_bp`, `strike_cooldown_ticks`, `strike_hold_runs`, `unfold_lo`, `unfold_hi`, `lurk_standoff_px`, `lurk_dwell_ticks`, the L3 constants, the mark and rig asset ids. The data lint refuses any field named `damage`, `accuracy`, `armour`, `dps`, `xp`, `unlock`, `health`, `hp`, `kill`, `loot`, `threat`, `aggro` or `hate` (Horror's own harm field is `strike_bp`, a Suit-scale amount, never `damage`). *Why.* Coding standards (gameplay values are data-driven) and the Item DB's lint AP-2; the field list is also the anti-combat guard (HE-38). *Cites.* IDB:97.
145	
146	**HE-6. Boundaries.** *Rule.* Horror does not read or write Attention's level, does not call `set_beacon`, does not schedule a breach, does not add a Graph footprint kind, does not read any `PERCEPTION_OUT` block, does not move, push or stagger a player (the stagger is the Controller's response to the Suit rung), places no content, narrates nothing, calls no physics query, owns no sound, mix or cue name, owns no HUD element, and holds no stimulus tracker, accumulator, "awareness", "alert", "threat" or "aggro" value, persisted or derived. *Why.* Guard rail 1: absorbing Attention is the most likely way this GDD drifts; the grep of this document for those words outside a negation returns zero (Acceptance Criteria lint).
147	
148	#### Group B — Permission, tell composition and the audit
149	
150	**HE-7. Phase-sourced behaviour, no stored drive.** *Rule.* Every transition between LURK and STALK, and every harm gate, is a function of `attention.view` fields only: `phase`, `tell_epoch`, `tell_outcome`, `locus_section_id`, `exogenous_permitted(section)`, `breach_enter_T`, `phase_enter_T`. The target (HE-13) is recomputed from physical `lux` on every run and is **not persisted**. The only things the record remembers are where it is, what state it is in since when, what it has already done this `tell_epoch` (counts), the locked point of a REACH in flight, and the stream counter. **Debug surface** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: a lethal AI cannot be playtested blind)*: each run also publishes a **non-persisted, non-hashed record `horror.view.debug`** on Horror's registered diagnostics channel (Debug Overlay DO-12, dev builds only), holding the current target ref or ANCHOR with each candidate's `lux_pm`, the goal room and the surrogate goal, the next hop, the transition guard that fired (1 to 7) and the HE-14 condition (a) to (f) that failed last, `hold_runs`, `blocked_runs`, `horror_wedged`, and the `linked` and `connected` results for the nearest seat *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. It is derived from the run, never read back: **no SIM rule, guard, formula or hash input may read `horror.view.debug`** (a lint, AC-HE-135), it is absent from `horror.state`, and it is never an accessibility or player surface (UI Requirements). *Why.* AT-2 (one level for the world), Pillar 1 (no hidden stat), guard rail 1. *Cites.* AT:139, AT:214-232.
151	
152	**HE-8. The permission predicate, repeated at three check points.** *Rule.* Every web-originated harm call (M17 RUPTURE, M17 GOUGE, `apply_suit_damage`) is made only if `exogenous_permitted(section)` holds **at the call tick**, where for a bodily hit `section` is Body's `actor_section(seat)` (crew-body scope, AT-15 R15; not the Graph's `section_of`) and for a hull deposit it is the section of the hull segment. The three check points are: (1) **REACH begin** (HE-14 condition c), (2) **STRIKE entry** (HE-15), (3) **every M17 RUPTURE or GOUGE call** (HE-16, HE-29). **CHILL is a non-harm footprint, permitted in any phase, bounded by HE-F4 and HE-31** (C-HE-28). A REACH may *begin* only in BREACH (not SUBSIDING); an in-flight REACH resolves only if the predicate still holds at its last tick, otherwise it fizzles with no harm, no hairlines, no GOUGE or RUPTURE (a touch-down smear already laid at the hold stage stays: it is true; a fizzle before the hold stage lays none) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Horror issues no STRESS (Attention's alone, AT-11). The registered formula `tell_window_contract` is the audit: for every harm event `e` there is an epoch `k` with `tell_start_k + tell_len_k <= t_e < subside_end_k`, `tell_len_k >= TELL_MIN_TICKS` and `section_e` in `locus_body_k` (the epoch's locus body in force at `t_e`: recorded at TELL entry, replaced only by an AT-14 fallback that TellAudit records as LOCUS_FALLBACK); zero violations over a replay. This GDD **repeats** AT-15; it does not restate a different rule. *Cites.* AT:211, REG `tell_window_contract`, AT:794-810.
153	
154	**HE-9. Tell composition: additive layers, never a substitute.** *Rule.* The Graph's 10-30 s requirement (LSG:144, LSG:1063) is met by **Attention's window** (AT-15); nothing in Horror shortens it, defers it or replaces it. Horror adds layers on top, and a harm path that skips one of them is a defect:
155	
156	| Layer | Owner | Duration | What the player can perceive | Present for |
157	|---|---|---|---|---|
158	| L0 Attention tell | Attention | `TELL_MIN_TICKS` 600 to `TELL_MAX_TICKS` 1800 | beats, filaments, dust, lamp gutter, audio (Attention's) | every harm path |
159	| L1 Presence and stalk | Horror | from ingress (at least `INGRESS_DELAY_TICKS` after TELL entry) or from TELL entry if already resident, to the first REACH | the entity in light, marks, disturbance dips, audio facts | bodily and hull paths |
160	| L2 REACH telegraph | Horror | `UNFOLD_TICKS` per strike, 95 to 180 ticks | the limb entering the cone before the body, tip resting on the locked point | every strike |
161	| L3 Footprint trail | Horror | continuous, any phase | smear, rime, hairlines | all |
162	| L4 Hull "scrape" | Horror | at least `min_gap` (> `STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS`, HE-F15) before a RUPTURE, because the RUPTURE needs the segment in `gouged_seg_ids` from an earlier strike *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | a GOUGE with radial hairlines on the same segment (HE-16) | RUPTURE only |
163	
164	The kernel's illustrative `rng_int(600, 1800)` on the stream name `"horror.tell"` (KRN D.10) is **not** Horror's tell length and not Horror's REACH range; the stream `"attention.tell"` is Attention's. Horror draws from `"horror.tell"` only the REACH length (HE-14). *Cites.* LSG:144, AT:211, KRN D.10, reflexion entry on examples read as contracts.
165	
166	**HE-10. TellAudit and the crew-body scope.** *Rule.* Horror publishes in `horror.view` the facts a `TellAudit` replay needs for every harm event (HE-37: `strike_T`, the seats hit, the hull segments gouged or ruptured, the `tell_epoch` it ran in) and submits no harm that the predicate would reject. A lethal act on a crew body outside a told breach is exactly the ambush Pillar 2 forbids, and Horror's stalk is additive and never a substitute. A restored CALM save never contains a lethal horror adjacent to a seat (CALM is non-lethal by construction, HE-11), so autosave needs no Horror-specific gate (SL-5 unchanged); if HE-11 is ever relaxed, SL-5 must be revisited. *Cites.* AT:211, SL:190.
167	
168	#### Group C — The behaviour cycle
169	
170	**HE-11. LURK: the non-lethal CALM presence.** *Rule.* In CALM a resident record is in LURK in its current body. It loiters at `V_CREEP_MPX` between waypoints drawn from Layout `anchor_geometry`: it dwells `LURK_DWELL_TICKS` at a waypoint, then the next waypoint is the lowest-hash candidate (`he_hash(entity_id, dwell_index, anchor_local_key, SALT_WP)`, HE-42; the chosen waypoint is held in the persisted `goal_wp` and the dwell start in `dwell_start_T`, HE-41) among waypoints in loaded sections of its body that are at least `LURK_STANDOFF_PX` from every living seat. It **never starts a move that brings it, or leaves it, nearer than `LURK_STANDOFF_PX` to a living seat** (the invariant is on the horror's own motion: a seat that walks toward it closes the gap itself, and the horror then steps away along the room graph; if cornered it holds still and does nothing). **Every `LURK_STANDOFF_PX` comparison in this rule (the standoff, the step-away and the waypoint filter) applies only to a seat for which `linked(horror, seat)` holds (HE-19)**: a room-level test that does not change while both stand in their rooms, so a horror at a doorway cannot oscillate between the standoff and step-away rules on a jamb graze, and a seat two short rooms away in open line of sight is linked; a seat in an unlinked room behind a wall does not push it away and is not a reason to hold still *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. It deposits no RUPTURE and no GOUGE and applies no suit damage; it may be seen, lays marks (HE-30), makes CHILL deposits (HE-27) and disturbance dips (HE-35). A seat may walk through it (no collision, BDY-17); that costs nothing and is a free moment of inspection. Its transitions out of LURK come **only from `attention.view.phase`**, never from the player's light, noise or distance. *Why.* Attention's "CALM is never known-safe" (AT:92, AT:373) is a claim about the phase (a TELL can begin at any time), not a claim that this presence can hurt, and this rule does not imply one: the CALM presence is provably harmless (no harm call, the standoff, the step-away) and **what a CALM sighting is worth is information**: which body it lives in (`RETURN_HOME`), and that its trail and rime are fresh (stage-0 marks), so the player may change the route, the lamp or the first job. It is not made dangerous to keep the dread up, because a harm in CALM would arrive with no tell and break Pillar 2; the standoff and the phase-only transitions also keep it from becoming a timer or a second meter (AT-2). Validation target (7) measures whether the information is used (AC-HE-122); if it is not, the first lever is `RETURN_HOME` 0 (OQ-1), never relaxing this rule. *Cites.* AT:92, AT:373.
171	
172	**HE-12. STALK: creep in a TELL, hunt in a BREACH.** *Rule.* On a TELL entry (a `tell_epoch` different from the record's `last_seen_tell_epoch`; **this comparison is the first evaluation for every record in every run, ahead of the dormancy guard**, States and Transitions guard 2) a record whose body holds the locus goes LURK → STALK; a record in another body goes LURK → TRANSIT (HE-20), **even when its own body is unloaded** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. In a TELL, STALK moves toward the target (HE-13) at `V_CREEP_MPX` and stops at `LURK_STANDOFF_PX` from every living seat that is `linked` to it (HE-19) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; it deposits no RUPTURE and no GOUGE and calls no `apply_suit_damage`. In BREACH it moves at `V_HUNT_MPX` and closes to `REACH_RANGE_PX` of the target point. STALK is one state; the speed is a function of `attention.view.phase`. **A TELL abort** (the phase leaves TELL with an aborted `tell_outcome`) returns STALK to LURK with no strike and no mark burst, and **cancels an outbound TRANSIT** (HE-20) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Entering SUBSIDING sends STALK to RETREAT. *Why.* Pillar 2 (the stalk is the additive earlier layer) and Pillar 3. *Cites.* AT:373, AT-16.
173	
174	**HE-13. Target from physical light.** *Rule.* Candidates are living seats (not DOWNED, DEAD or IN_POD per the Controller's `loco_state`) whose `actor_section` is in `locus_body` (TELL, BREACH, SUBSIDING) or in the record's own body (CALM). One `lux(ref)` read per candidate per run, zero probes. **The target rule, stated plainly** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: a candidate is *lit* when its total light `lux_pm(s) >= LIT_ON_PM` (150, CITED), a stateless comparison on the same quantity the argmax uses (the comparison is made fresh every run and nothing is stored; there is no off-threshold and no hysteresis, as for the Emitter's `probe` `lit_on`). **Horror does not gate on the Emitter's `lit` bit**: that bit is a hysteresis on `act_lux_pm`, which excludes the owner's own beam (EM-2, EM-21, EM AC-16a), so a lone player in the dark with the lamp on reads `lux_pm` 1000 but `act_lux_pm` 0 and would never be a candidate; the Emitter's own wording ("Horror sees a lit player", EM line 685) is the contract. Any light that raises `lux_pm` counts, including a fixture (the self-powered status glow of a docked pod's dock-room prop is an ordinary lit fixture by user ruling X2, so a seat at the dock console is a lit candidate and Horror adds no exception for it *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*), a node lantern, a Chemlight pool, another crewmate's beam and the BEACON's sweep (the BEACON does not gate actions but does count in `lux_pm`; a seat swept by it is lit for as long as `lux_pm` stays at or above the threshold, and because P locks at REACH start a flapping lit state cannot steer a strike). **A seat standing in fixture light is lit and can be targeted with its own lamp off**; going dark means leaving the light, not only switching the lamp off (HE-26). The target is the lit candidate with the highest `lux_pm`, ties lowest seat id. **The argmax is therefore degenerate among seats whose own lamp is on**: each reads 1000 (the owner stands in their own light, EM-21), so the lowest seat id wins; the argmax discriminates only among seats lit by *other* light (fixtures, pools, a teammate's beam), and it is the presence of light, not its amount, that draws the horror. If no candidate is lit, the target is the locus section's anchor (the anchor REACH of HE-16). **The preference is recomputed every run and never stored.** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* The *walk* it leads to is committed, the target is not: the chosen goal waypoint is held in the persisted `goal_wp` for `GOAL_COMMIT_RUNS` runs (12, 60 ticks) unless it is reached, its seat leaves the candidate set, the phase changes, the layout changes or the goal becomes unreachable, so a lone seat on a lux boundary or under an L3 dip cannot make the stalk dither at 12 Hz (the layer players read as "it was hunting me"); REACH begin (HE-14) always reads the fresh target. The horror moves identically lit or unlit and is never repelled, stunned, slowed or harmed by light. This GDD **adopts the Emitter's text verbatim**, as the second GDD to land: "No beam stuns, burns, repels or damages a horror or a crewmate ... being revealed is the beam's whole effect" (EM:89). Objects are never targets at MVP: a dropped glowstick is a Chemlight pool that counts as exposure to whoever stands in it, but it is not a seat, so it does not pull the horror toward itself; flares, torches and decoys that repel or distract are Vertical Slice (EM:89). *Why.* Pillar 3 made legible ("you lit up, it came") with no meter. With two or more lit seats a stateless argmax can alternate; a hysteresis would need a stored value, which is a Vertical Slice question (Open Questions). *Cites.* EM:89, EM-21.
175	
176	**HE-14. REACH: the telegraph (unfold).** *Rule.* STALK → REACH begins at a run when **all** of the following hold: (a) `phase` is BREACH; (b) the target is a lit seat, or the anchor under HE-16; (c) `exogenous_permitted(actor_section(target seat))` holds for a seat REACH, and `exogenous_permitted(anchor section)` holds for an anchor REACH; (d) the distance from the horror's foot point to the point is at most `REACH_RANGE_PX`; (e) `T >= cooldown_until_T`; **(f) `connected(horror foot, P)`** (HE-19): the horror's foot point and P are in the same room (Layout `room_at`), or the two rooms are adjacent through an open, passable leaf (Layout `door_passage`, HE-19) whose hinge-aware `gap_rect` the straight segment from the foot point to P crosses *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. A Euclidean distance through a wall is not a reach: a horror one tile behind a wall from a lit seat begins no REACH, and the same pair across an open sill does *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: condition (d) alone let a REACH start through solid wall and strike nothing, a telegraph drawn through a wall for a lethal mechanic, which breaks P2's "a careful player could have perceived and had somewhere to run")*. The same condition (f) gates the anchor REACH (HE-16 (3)). At that run it **locks** the point P (the target seat's foot point; non-tracking) and draws `UNFOLD_TICKS = 5 × ceil_div(rng_int(UNFOLD_LO/5, UNFOLD_HI/5) × UNFOLD_SCALE_PCT, 100)` (integer order of operations: draw, multiply by the scale, `ceil_div`, then × 5) from `rng_derive_epoch(world_seed, "horror.tell", counter)` (the kernel's one restore-epoch derivation, HE-42) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: kernel name `rng_derive_epoch`)* (`UNFOLD_SCALE_PCT` is the accessibility lengthening of HE-F5, default 100, persisted in `horror.state`; it is applied after the draw, never shortens, and does not change the draw count) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; the counter increments in the same block write, is persisted and restored exactly, and a restore never rerolls a REACH already in flight (its length is the stored `reach_end_T`; a REACH that later fizzles has still consumed its draw); the next REACH after a restore draws at the restored counter with the restore's new `restore_epoch` inside `rng_derive_epoch` (HE-42) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: kernel name `rng_derive_epoch`)* The body is rooted for the whole REACH; the limb extends toward P; `reach_end_T = reach_start_T + UNFOLD_TICKS` is a multiple of 5, so the strike resolves exactly on a run. During REACH the record publishes `state`, `locked_pt` and `reach_end_T` in `horror.view` (the rig and Audio read them). `UNFOLD_LO` and `UNFOLD_HI` must be multiples of 5 (data lint). The picture is the warning: the rig's reach-limb tip rests on P for the last part of the unfold (Visual/Audio Requirements), and the telegraph is **the limb entering the cone before the body**; no icon, ring, arc, disc, radius or ground decal marks the strike point. **The tip rests on P, which is the victim's own foot point, inside the victim's own light (EM-21: the owner stands in their own light), so the tip is lit for the victim wherever the body stands**; a touch-down SMEAR is laid at P at the start of the **hold stage** (`hold_start_T = reach_end_T − 5 × floor(3 × (UNFOLD_TICKS / 5) / 10)`, the last 25 to 50 ticks, when the tip rests on P; a true mark and a ring entry, not a marker) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: it is laid late on purpose, because a ground cue at REACH start would be a second, unacknowledged warning beside the limb and would weaken the blind-legibility claim (the limb alone carries the telegraph); a REACH that fizzles before the hold stage lays no smear, and `reach_start_T` and `locked_pt` stay observable in `horror.view` and the debug record so replay and TellAudit still see when the REACH began; Audio renders a positional REACH cue from `locked_pt`: a non-percussive lead-in started `REACH_RESOLVE_PRE_TICKS` 90 before `reach_end_T` (registry `reach_resolve_start`, `REACH_RESOLVE_PRE_TICKS <= UNFOLD_LO`) and ending at `reach_end_T` with no impact transient (Audio AA-28 b). There is **no lit-self gate**: the horror moves identically lit or unlit (HE-13). The point is locked at the start and never updated, so moving out of the strike disc (HE-15) always works. If the blind-legibility acceptance criterion fails, the fallback is a larger `UNFOLD_LO` or a smaller `R_SNAP_PX`, never a victim-side marker (a marker is a HUD by another name, Pillar 3). *(orchestrator ruling: checkpoint CP-1; C-HE-9 closed.)* *Why.* ART 5.4 ("a limb entering the cone before the body"), Pillar 2; a tracking strike is learnable never. *Cites.* HE-F2, HE-F5, ART:540.
177	
178	**HE-15. STRIKE: bodily resolution.** *Rule.* At the first run with `T >= reach_end_T` and the predicate satisfied, the state becomes STRIKE for `STRIKE_HOLD_RUNS` runs (the snap pose; no travel). On the entry run, for **every** living, non-DOWNED, non-DEAD seat whose `actor_section` is the section of P, whose room (Layout `room_at`) equals the room of P, whose foot point is **strictly within** `R_SNAP_PX` of P (`dist < R_SNAP_PX`), and for which `exogenous_permitted(actor_section(seat))` holds at that tick, Horror calls `apply_suit_damage(player_id, STRIKE_BP, source_ref = the horror's ref)` once. `apply_suit_damage` is the 3-argument Suit mutator; the class (EXOGENOUS) travels on `source_ref`, classed EXOGENOUS once at record creation (boot or ingress arrival), persisted with the record, and valid across restore independently of E6 (SE:322, SE-23; persisted as `exo_source_class`, HE-41); an unclassed ref is a programmer error. The room test stops a strike through a wall. A seat standing on a door sill belongs to the sill's room (Layout `room_at`). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* The strike's wall test is the **strict same-room clause only**: the second branch of `connected` (an adjacent room across an open, passable sill, HE-19) applies to REACH begin and nowhere in the strike, so a seat in the adjacent room across an open sill is spared even though a REACH could begin toward it (AC-HE-27). The strike is target-agnostic *within a body REACH*: any living seat in the disc is hit, whether or not it was the target. `STRIKE_BP` 3200 satisfies HE-F3 (strike one: 10000 → 6800, below `SUIT_HP_OK`, rung STRAINED; strike two → 3600, below `SUIT_LEAK_HP`, CRITICAL, stagger, walk-only; strike three → 400, below `SUIT_HP_FAIL`, FAILED → DOWNED → `DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS` 1800 → DEAD, Suit's ladder, Save/Load's restore). Each exogenous harm lands through `apply_suit_damage(..., EXOGENOUS)` only after the horror's own 10-30 s tell (HE-9). Horror assumes `SUIT_EXO_BYPASS_LIMITER` 1 (an EXOGENOUS hit sets the integrity rung from `integrity_bp` with no limiter hold; Interaction's IA-31 now quotes the default 1, matching the registry: C-HE-5 closed 2026-10-27). Horror never moves, pushes or staggers a seat. A STRIKE publishes `strike_T` and the seats hit (HE-37) as the hit cue, because Suit's STRAINED rung is inert and carries no witness of its own (SE:83, SE:129). **The hit mark.** On the same entry run, if `apply_suit_damage` was actually called at least once, Horror lays exactly one **STRUCK** mark at P (HE-27, HE-30); if it was called for no seat, no STRUCK mark is laid. A touch-down SMEAR laid at the hold stage is on the floor whether or not the strike lands (HE-30), so without the STRUCK mark the floor would look the same after a hit and after a miss; with it the floor records a hit, and a death has a post-hoc cause the player can read (validation target 1). The mark is a true ring entry written by the same run that struck, never a marker and never read back as a hidden value. *Why.* The user's decision ("death is a bitch. It happens.") bounded to three told strikes. **Strike one is not a visible rung:** Suit's integrity STRAINED (`SUIT_LEAK_HP <= integrity_bp < SUIT_HP_OK`) is inert and has no witness by design (Suit's creative-director review chose none; reversal path SE OQ-19). Strike one is therefore witnessed by the strike itself (snap pose, Audio's positional strike cue from `strike_T`), by Suit's integrity reading, and by the STRUCK mark that stays on the floor after the moment has passed (a miss leaves only the touch-down smear); the first physical consequence is strike two (leak, seam jet, CRITICAL, stagger, walk-only). A hit that left no trace anywhere would be a hidden stat (Pillar 1), which is why the strike itself carries the witness and the floor keeps it: the pipe, not the number. *Cites.* SE:322, SE:221, SE:223, HE-F2, HE-F3.
179	
180	**HE-16. Hull acts: GOUGE, RUPTURE and the anchor REACH.** *Rule.* (1) *Hull GOUGE with a strike.* If P lies within `HULL_CONTACT_PX` of a hull-segment face, the STRIKE entry run also deposits GOUGE (`deposit_trace(GOUGE, hull_segment_id, magnitude <= FOOTPRINT_MAX_GOUGE_BP)`) on that segment, at most `GOUGES_PER_EPOCH_MAX` per `tell_epoch`, appends the segment id to `gouged_seg_ids` if absent (HE-41) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, and lays radial hairlines at the contact point. **GOUGE subjects are hull segments only** (binding on this GDD by the creative-director's CD-GDD-ALIGN ruling, FT-31 and FT:1412): a duct, cable, pipe or door is never a GOUGE subject (lint `GOUGE_NON_HULL`). (2) *RUPTURE.* A RUPTURE (`deposit_trace(RUPTURE, hull_segment_id, ...)`, hull only) is issued only on a STRIKE whose P is within `HULL_CONTACT_PX` of a hull segment that is **in `gouged_seg_ids`, that is, already carries a Horror GOUGE from an earlier strike this epoch** (always at least `min_gap` > `STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS` earlier, HE-F15, so the scrape precedes the tear by a full told cycle, layer L4 of HE-9; no stored timestamp is needed, because a time clause could never decide an outcome) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, and at most `RUPTURES_PER_EPOCH_MAX` 1 per epoch, **and only when the strike's disc holds no living seat at resolution (the HE-15 hit list is empty)**: a RUPTURE never lands on a struck seat, so the compound case "a seat already CRITICAL and staggered, hit again, with a hull breach opening beside it" cannot occur; a strike that hits someone deposits a GOUGE at most, and the RUPTURE is spent only when the target walked out and the ship pays instead ("I lived, and the ship paid") *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: a RUPTURE on a victim already CRITICAL and staggered is the most lethal combination in the design and HE-F16 did not model it; modelling the Suit and Graph compound belongs to those documents, so this GDD excludes it by construction; see Open Question 2 for the rejected alternative; the miss-only rule is a user ruling, 2026-10-27)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. Each act has its own REACH and its own predicate check. (3) *Anchor REACH (no lit seat).* With no lit candidate the target is the locus section's anchor: **the lowest-id anchor (Layout `anchor_geometry`) of the locus section's outermost compartment that lies within `HULL_CONTACT_PX` of a hull-segment face; if there is none, the REACH lays hairlines only.** The horror stalks to `REACH_RANGE_PX` of it and runs a REACH whose resolution lays radial hairlines and, because `ANCHOR_REACH_GOUGES` defaults to 1, **one hull GOUGE** (hull only, under `GOUGES_PER_EPOCH_MAX`, never RUPTURE, never `apply_suit_damage`). Its `fatigued` creep is ENDOGENOUS and told by the Graph's own gate (P2 holds), so going dark now costs the ship (AT-11, Pillar 5). *(orchestrator ruling: checkpoint CP-4; C-HE-24 resolved.)* (4) *The Graph's consequence is the Graph's.* A GOUGE sets the segment `fatigued` (LSG M17 row); the creep it starts is an ENDOGENOUS clock that outlives the breach and sits under the Graph's own `W_MIN_WARNING_S` gate. Horror neither alters nor shortens it. (5) *Read published.* Mapping P to a Graph hull-segment id uses Layout's `hull_segments_near(section_id, px, r) -> [HULL_SEGMENT node id]` (node ids ascending, Chebyshev distance `r` to the plate-position face span; Layout LY-28 reads): C-HE-11 is closed 2026-10-27 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; was provisional)*. *Why.* R2: the physical half of the footprint grammar, hull-only, bounded per epoch; the "scrape then tear" ladder keeps even a hull RUPTURE preceded by a told GOUGE. *(Open Question: whether RUPTURE belongs in the anchor ladder at all; at the default it does not, so RUPTURE is reachable only when a REACH on a lit seat beside a hull face that already carries this epoch's Horror GOUGE resolves with nobody inside the disc, that is, when the seat has walked out.)* *Cites.* FT:199, FT:1412, LSG:196.
181	
182	**HE-17. RETREAT, cooldown and SUBSIDING.** *Rule.* After a STRIKE the state is RETREAT: the horror moves at `V_CREEP_MPX` along the room graph to the nearest waypoint at least `LURK_STANDOFF_PX` from every living seat, and `cooldown_until_T = strike_T + STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS` (invariant `STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS > STAGGER_TICKS` 30, CITED). A **fizzle** (the predicate fails at the REACH's last tick, the phase has returned to CALM, or a restore finds the predicate false) goes to RETREAT with no harm, no hairlines, no GOUGE or RUPTURE and **no cooldown consumed**, so a fizzle cannot starve the next legitimate REACH; **a touch-down smear already laid at the hold stage stays** (it is true; a fizzle before the hold stage lays none) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. RETREAT → STALK when `T >= cooldown_until_T` and `phase` is BREACH; RETREAT → LURK when the phase is CALM or TELL and the record is not returning home. In SUBSIDING no new REACH starts and STALK goes to RETREAT; an in-flight REACH that reaches `reach_end_T` during SUBSIDING **resolves** (the predicate holds in SUBSIDING for sections in `locus_body`, so TellAudit passes) and then RETREATs, unless the knob `SUBSIDE_CANCELS_REACH` is 1 (the merciful variant, default 0). *(orchestrator ruling: this reconciles the two clauses "SUBSIDING sends the horror to RETREAT" and "an in-flight REACH resolves iff the predicate holds at its last tick" as resolve-then-RETREAT; ambiguity C-HE-10.)* Pod-hop: the departed seat leaves `locus_body`, so `exogenous_permitted(actor_section(seat))` fails and an in-flight REACH on it fizzles; on a derelict locus, the departure of the last occupant recorded at BREACH entry also ends the breach (AT-12 (iii)). *Cites.* AT:200, AT:203, SE-24.
