184	**HE-18. Never harm what is already down.** *Rule.* DOWNED and DEAD seats are not candidates (HE-13) and are skipped at resolution (HE-15). After the third strike the seat is DOWNED and the clock `DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS` is the Controller's and Suit's (SE-24); death and restore belong to Save/Load (SL-7). Horror owns only the act and its tell. A seat that becomes DOWNED or DEAD during a REACH is not hit; the REACH completes harmlessly (the telegraph was already told) and the record RETREATs. *Cites.* SE:223, SL:197.
185	
186	**HE-19. Strike scope is geometry, not intent.** *Rule.* Resolution reads only Layout `room_at`, `room_adjacency` (open or closed leaf), `door_passage`, the horror's and the seats' integer positions, and `solid_in` for the horror's own movement. No `probe()` and no physics query. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **The Layout read for door geometry, `door_passage(section_id, via_id)`** (published: Layout LY-28 and D.5, AC-180) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. `via_id` is the `room_adjacency` record's `via_id` (Layout's `door_index`). It returns `{orientation EW|NS, sill_rect, gap_rect, open_extent_px}`: pure, integer, section-local base px; rects are Layout's OUT convention, the occupied span (x0, y0, x1−1, y1−1); `sill_rect` is the door cell rectangle; `gap_rect` is NONE when `open_extent_px` is 0. Data path: the Graph's `opening(edge_id) = {area, area_max, door_state}` → Layout's `layout.doors` (P3, runs before `body.integrate`, which runs before `horror.step`, so a run sees same-tick state) → `open_extent_px = floor_div(96 × area, area_max)`; Horror never calls `opening()` and owns no door state. `gap_rect` is **hinge-aware** (for a partially open leaf the open part lies on the side away from the hinge, so it is not centred on the sill). A leaf is *passable* iff `open_extent_px >= foot_extent(orientation)`, with `foot_extent` = `FOOT_BOX_W` 16 across an E-W wall run and `FOOT_BOX_H` 8 across a N-S wall run (Body's foot box, cited; Layout's `passes(F)`; the foot box is 16 wide and 8 deep, so a single 16 px threshold is wrong for one of the two orientations). The result changes only when `version(section_id)` changes, so HE-25's cache key is unchanged. There is no `solid_in` sampling fallback, because the five `solid_in` queries per run (HE-43) already belong to movement. **The segment test, stated once:** the straight integer segment a → b crosses `gap_rect` iff it meets the closed occupied span [x0, x1−1] × [y0, y1−1] (integer cross-multiplication; no ray, no float, no physics query). **Two room predicates, split on purpose.** (1) `linked(a, b)`, for every Horror *movement* distance rule: true iff `room_hops(room_at(a), room_at(b)) <= LINK_ROOM_HOPS` (default 2, range 1 to 3) over the room graph whose edges are the DOOR and HATCH records of `room_adjacency` with `open_extent_px > 0` (open at all, whatever the width). It depends only on the two room ids and the open or closed state of the doors, so it is constant while both stand in their rooms: a horror at a doorway cannot flip between the standoff and the step-away rule from a one-pixel move, and a seat two short rooms away in open line of sight is linked; a door opening or closing flips it as one discrete event. (2) `connected(a, b)`, for REACH begin only (HE-14 (f)): true iff `room_at(a) == room_at(b)`, or the two rooms are adjacent through a DOOR or HATCH record whose leaf is *passable* and the straight integer segment `a → b` crosses that record's `gap_rect` (the segment test above). The strike's wall test (HE-15) is stricter than both, **strictly the same room**, so the second branch of `connected` never reaches a seat. `linked` is the test for the `LURK_STANDOFF_PX` standoff and step-away tests of HE-11, HE-12 and HE-17, the waypoint filter of HE-11, and the standoff clause of the ingress legality test of HE-20 and HE-F9; `connected` is the test for REACH condition (f) and for the anchor REACH. A door waypoint (HE-25) is the centre of `gap_rect`. The straight segment from the horror's foot point to P must not cross a closed door leaf (checked through the room-graph sill, not a ray). The same-room test (HE-15) is re-evaluated at resolution against the *current* layout, so a weld or cut during a REACH is honoured while the locked point stays the same physical point (the stored integer, translated only by HE-22's frame re-base) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*.
187	
188	#### Group D — Presence: ingress, TRANSIT, return, dormancy, weld and cut
189	
190	**HE-20. Instance, ingress, TRANSIT, egress and return.** *Rule.* The record has a **home body** (default: derelict B, the web-intrusion side, DA OQ-V5). At TELL entry (observed as `tell_epoch != last_seen_tell_epoch`, the **first evaluation of every record in every run, ahead of dormancy**; transition guard 2), if `body_of(locus_section_id)` is not the record's body, the record leaves its body **whether or not that body is loaded** (E7 `unregister_subject` only if the ref is still registered, because HE-34 already unregistered it when the body unloaded; an egress mark at the old position, inserted into the block-level ring with the old, possibly unloaded, `section_id` and not ageing until that section loads, HE-21; the departed-from body is stored as `from_body_id`), enters `TRANSIT` with `transit_until_T = tell_enter_T + INGRESS_DELAY_TICKS` (the destination body, `transit_to_body_id`, is the locus body), and arrives at a hull segment of the locus body chosen by HE-F9: the compartment **one room hop from the room of the highest-`lux_pm` living seat in the locus body** (none lit or none present: the locus section's outermost compartment; ties lowest room id, then lowest hull-segment id), **never a room holding a living seat and never inside `LURK_STANDOFF_PX` of a living seat that is `linked` to the entry (HE-19)**, no earlier than `INGRESS_DELAY_TICKS` after TELL entry *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. The candidate entries are composed from published Layout reads only: a *hull entry* is an `anchor_geometry` point (section-local, composed with `section_offset`) of a hull-bearing compartment of the locus body that lies within `HULL_CONTACT_PX` of a hull face, paired with the lowest id returned by `hull_segments_near(section_id, anchor_px, HULL_CONTACT_PX)`; there is no `solid_in` sampling and no unpublished room-to-segment read, and the chosen `ingress_seg`, `ingress_anchor_px` and `ingress_mark_T` are persisted (HE-41). The ingress mark (smear and radial hairlines at the segment) is laid `INGRESS_MARK_LEAD_TICKS` before the body appears, so a player looking at that wall sees the arrival coming; on arrival the record registers (E6) and enters STALK (or LURK if the phase is already CALM for a reason other than an abort, for example a return home completing; an abort cancels an outbound arrival instead, see below) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. **This departure is the one exemption from HE-21's dormancy** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the default home body is derelict B, which is usually not the body the player is on, so without the exemption a record whose own body is unloaded would be frozen by its own dormancy rule at the first TELL on the home ship or derelict A and a told breach would have no horror in it: cry-wolf, Pillar 1's "the tell is a promise")*. A record already in TRANSIT that sees a new `tell_epoch` retargets: `transit_to_body_id` becomes the new locus body and `transit_until_T` is recomputed from the new TELL entry. **TELL abort while in TRANSIT:** if the phase leaves TELL with an aborted outcome while the record is outbound (it has not yet arrived), the arrival is cancelled, nothing is injected into the player's body, and the record heads back: `transit_to_body_id` becomes `from_body_id` (with `RETURN_HOME` 1 the home body), `transit_leg` becomes RETURN (it is OUTBOUND while heading for a locus body, including after a retarget to a new locus, and RETURN while heading home), `transit_until_T = abort_T + RETURN_DELAY_TICKS`, and the arrival at that body follows HE-21 (it waits if that body is unloaded); an ingress mark already laid stays (it is a true mark) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: an abort must send a restraint signal, not inject a CALM presence into the ship that held its fire)*. If no entry is legal the record stays in TRANSIT and retries each run (diagnostic `horror_ingress_pending`; a record still unregistered after the first Horror run at or after BREACH entry is a cry-wolf defect and an acceptance criterion; a record that registers on that run, at most 4 ticks after BREACH entry by run alignment, E-HE-17, is not) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **The rule relaxes so a told breach cannot pass with nothing in it:** at `tell_enter_T + INGRESS_DELAY_TICKS + STALK_VISIBLE_FLOOR_TICKS` (540 at the placeholders) the entry rule falls back to the *nearest legal hull anchor* (HE-F9: the hop-1 and standoff conditions drop out; the entry is the hull entry nearest by room hops to the lit seat's room whose room holds no living seat), whose mark is laid at once and whose body arrives `INGRESS_MARK_LEAD_TICKS` later, at the first Horror run at or after `TELL_MIN_TICKS` (at most 4 ticks later for an unaligned `tell_enter_T`, E-HE-17) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; only when every hull room holds a living seat does the record stay pending (AC-HE-44). **Return:** when `RETURN_HOME` is 1 (default [PH]), `RETURN_DELAY_TICKS` after SUBSIDING ends or after a TELL abort the record returns to its home body by the same rule (no seat target: the home body's outermost compartment, lowest ids; the legality tests still apply); when `RETURN_HOME` is 0 it does not return and LURKs in the body of the last breach (the creative-director's lean; an Open Question bound to validation target (2), the 70 % CALM sighting: if the target fails, flip this knob first). All choices are deterministic functions of Attention's locus, Emitter reads and ids; nothing is authored (DA:101 "authoring places no entity"). TRANSIT is unregistered, has no position, publishes `state` TRANSIT and `transit_until_T`, harms nothing and lays no marks. The fiction is that the web runs through hulls; both ends leave a mark. Whether a CALM presence aboard the home ship after a home-ship breach is acceptable is settled for MVP in Open Question 6: default `RETURN_HOME` 1, and the departure rule above makes the told breach independent of that knob (with `RETURN_HOME` 0 the record still leaves an unloaded body at every TELL elsewhere, so a TELL is never empty) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. *Why.* The first draft's "lowest-id hull segment of the outermost compartment" could place the entity rooms from the player and let it arrive late in BREACH (cry-wolf); one-hop ingress keeps teeth and keeps the approach told. *(orchestrator ruling: ingress refined to one room hop.)* *Cites.* DA:101, AT-12.
191	
192	**HE-21. Dormancy.** *Rule.* A record whose body is unloaded is frozen: no step, no mark ageing, no disturbance, **no fast-forward** (LS-17, LSG:174). **The single exemption is the TELL departure of HE-20** (the new-`tell_epoch` comparison runs before this rule, so an unloaded record whose body is not the locus body leaves for TRANSIT; it does nothing else) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. A mark's `life_left` falls only while the mark's section is loaded (an egress mark laid in an unloaded section is inserted at once and starts ageing when that section loads). A record in TRANSIT whose destination body unloads waits. Answer to Web Map ASK-H1: yes. A record may enter TRANSIT toward an unloaded body (for example a return home to derelict B while it is unloaded). It stays in TRANSIT, unregistered, with no position, no marks and no harm, and arrives at its first run after the body loads with a legal HE-20 entry. The transit machine's `TRANSIT_HOLD` and pod states are Web Map's and are never read as Horror's TRANSIT. *Cites.* LSG:174, LS-17, WM:458.
193	
194	**HE-22. Weld and cut.** *Rule.* The path cache is keyed by the layout (HE-25) and recomputed on any `layout.state` change (a weld or cut applying, MSA-14 / MSA-20). If a weld changes `locus_body` membership, the target body is re-derived from `locus_section_id` on the next run (`locus_body` is recorded at TELL entry and is replaced mid-epoch only by an AT-14 fallback, which TellAudit records as LOCUS_FALLBACK; Horror re-reads `locus_section_id` each run). If a cut removes the section the record stands in from its body, the record's `body_id` is re-derived from `body_of(section_id)`; if its section is gone the record goes to TRANSIT with an egress mark and re-enters its home body. **Re-basing the body-frame points** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: Layout owns the frame, G1/G6; a weld re-bases the absorbed body by `frame_shift_px`, Layout D.6, and the MVP horror's home body, derelict B, is the absorbed body)*: at the start of each run, if `section_offset(section_id)` or `body_of(section_id)` differs from the stored `offset_seen_px` / `body_id` (a weld or cut moved the record's section, Layout LY-16/LY-17), Horror re-bases every persisted body-frame point of the record (`pos_px`, `locked_pt`, `ingress_anchor_px` and any other body-frame px pair in HE-41 groups 1, 3 and 5; section-local fields such as `goal_wp` are untouched) by `delta = section_offset(section_id) − offset_seen_px`, re-derives `body_id` from `body_of(section_id)`, stores the new `offset_seen_px`, and calls E8 `set_subject_anchor(ref, pos_px)` in the same run. The Emitter derives the HORROR subject's `body_id` itself (EM-4, EM-21) and lands the new anchor at the next `emitter.place`. Horror has no cut verb and does not interrupt a cut; Modular Ship Assembly states the same ("Horror and Attention have no cut verb; the breach rhythm uses STRESS and M17, not detaches", MSA-22). *Cites.* MSA-14 / MSA-20 (weld and cut apply), MSA-22 (no cut verb).
195	
196	#### Group E — Movement and pathing
197	
198	**HE-23. Own position, Body's pure step.** *Rule.* Positions are Horror's, in integer base px with a two-axis sub-pixel residue and `last_octant`, inside `horror.state`. Movement calls Body's pure `LocomotionStep` (BDY-10) with `collide` bound to Layout `solid_in`, using Body's foot box (`FOOT_BOX_W` 16, `FOOT_BOX_H` 8, CITED; the 64 to 96 px sprite is visual only, because a larger box could never use an open doorway whose passage extent is exactly 16 across). Per run the horror picks one octant (the integer argmax of the eight unit vectors against the direction to the next waypoint, ties lowest octant) and steps once per tick for the five ticks of the run. There are no `AGENT` rows in Body at MVP (preserving `MAX_ACTORS` 8 headroom for Vertical Slice B seats), no `CharacterBody2D` and no physics query (CR-13 G3, H10). A horror's footprint is a Graph trail or a Horror mark, never a Body fact (BDY-4). `pos_prev` is the position at run start and `pos_curr` the position at run end. -> ADR candidate (1): horror position ownership versus Body `AGENT` rows. *Cites.* BDY-4, BDY-10, BDY-15.
199	
200	**HE-24. Speeds and the escape invariant.** *Rule.* Registered constants, in milli-px per tick: `V_CREEP_MPX` 1000 (LURK, STALK in a TELL, RETREAT, the arrival walk), `V_HUNT_MPX` 1500 (STALK in BREACH). Each tick adds the speed to an accumulator, steps `floor(acc / 1000)` px and keeps the remainder (persisted per record). Registered invariant (HE-F6): `V_CREEP_MPX < V_HUNT_MPX < V_WALK × 1000` (2000), so **a walking seat, including a CRITICAL walk-only seat, always outpaces it**, and there is no lunge travel (the strike resolves at the locked point). A seat that is *carrying* moves at `V_CARRY` 1 (CITED, BDY-13): `V_HUNT_MPX` exceeds it, so a carrier cannot out-walk the approach, and a carrier needs 72 ticks (73 on a diagonal octant) to clear the disc against 40 available (`UNFOLD_LO` 95 less 54 for reaction less 1 for command application; conflict C-HE-8), so **a carrier who does not drop the cargo is struck on 7 of the 18 draws (38.9 %)**: the intended answer is to drop the cargo and walk (Interaction's `drop` is a TAP, lit-exempt and uninterruptible, IA-28; it can only be refused `OBSTRUCTED` when no free cell exists, which is an authoring defect to be lint-covered and a cross-GDD note to Interaction), or accept the hit; the telegraph length is **not** tied to the seat's `V_CARRY` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the 38.9 % figure is now explicit rather than implicit, and the drop is the stated counterplay)*. *(orchestrator ruling: stated as intended; hauling is where the horror bites, Pillar 5 risk; the DA-29 wording note is an owed row.)* Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): 'drop the cargo' is confirmed as the intended price of hauling (a carrier who keeps the cargo is struck on 7 of 18 draws, 38.9 %); `R_SNAP_PX` stays 72 and 48 is the ruled lever (HE-F5, worked example) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *Cites.* DA-29, BDY-13, REG `V_CARRY`.
201	
202	**HE-25. Pathing over Layout reads.** *Rule.* The horror searches an integer room graph built from Layout `room_adjacency(section_id)` over every section of its body (`sections_of`), excluding any edge whose door leaf is closed or **not passable** (a *passable leaf* is open with `open_extent_px` at least the foot-box extent across its wall run, 16 px (`FOOT_BOX_W`) across an E-W wall and 8 px (`FOOT_BOX_H`) across a N-S wall, from Layout's `door_passage` (HE-19); a leaf opened to less is solid to the horror) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. Breadth-first by hop count, ties lowest room id, at most `PATH_EXPANSIONS_MAX` node expansions per run (HE-F10); the result is cached as a next-hop table per goal room and layout key. **One graph, one goal rule (the surrogate-goal BFS)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the text had defined the pathing graph two ways, an open-leaf BFS and the full adjacency truncated at a closed leaf)*: the goal room is chosen over the full adjacency (closed and impassable leaves counted for distance, E-HE-20); the search runs on the passable-leaf graph only; when the goal room is not reachable the *surrogate goal* is the reachable room with the smallest full-adjacency hop distance to the goal room (ties lowest room id), and the horror walks there and stops. Inside a room it steers by octant toward the next waypoint (the centre of a door's hinge-aware `gap_rect`, not the sill centre or the leaf, or an `anchor_geometry` point) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; a waypoint is **reached** when the foot point is within `ARRIVE_PX` (8 px [PH], at least the largest per-run displacement, 8 px at `V_HUNT_MPX`, so a run can never step over a waypoint) of it. There is no obstacle avoidance beyond the **local slide rule**, which uses only the persisted `blocked_runs` counter: when the previous run ended `blocked`, `blocked_runs` is 1 and the run uses the adjacent octant (±1) with the larger dot product against the direction to the waypoint (ties lowest octant); at `blocked_runs` 2 it uses the other adjacent octant; from 3 it returns to the direct octant. Authoring contract: a room's walkable floor must let straight octant steps between its sills and anchors succeed with at most this slide (lint `ROOM_NONCONVEX_PATH`, owed to Layout and Derelict Authoring; an L-shaped footprint fixture is AC-HE-128). On a NONE or UNKNOWN Layout read it holds its last waypoint for at most `HOLD_MAX_RUNS` (counted in the persisted `hold_runs`), and then **the fallback depends on the phase: in CALM and TELL it goes to LURK; in BREACH it stays in STALK and holds position (LURK is n/a in BREACH, so a hold-then-LURK there would break the phase view and leave a breach with a horror that cannot do harm); in SUBSIDING it goes to RETREAT**; a record in RETREAT holds in place in any phase *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; **UNKNOWN is never read as "unlit" or as "open"**. If `step` reports no movement for `BLOCKED_RUNS_MAX` consecutive runs it discards the cached hop and re-paths once; if it is still without movement after a second `BLOCKED_RUNS_MAX` runs it is **wedged**, and the defined outcome is RETREAT (counter `horror_wedged`, `cooldown_until_T := T`; in BREACH it then returns to STALK and re-paths, so a wedge repeats visibly in the diagnostics and is an authoring signal, never a silent permanent stall) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Zero `probe()` calls at MVP. `NavigationServer2D` and `NavigationAgent2D` are rejected (node- and server-based, outside the replay hash; H10, G3). `route_length_px` stays diagnostic (LY:310). Layout now states (ship-section-and-layout-data-model.md, LY-28 reads and LY-33) that `layout_hash()` does **not** cover door state and that a reader caching on door geometry keys on `version(section_id)`; the cache key is therefore `(goal_room, layout_hash, version(section_id) of every section of the body)`, a restore (where `version` resets) is an unconditional rebuild, and the Horror-computed closed-leaf hash is retired (C-HE-13 closed 2026-10-27, design review). -> ADR candidate (2). *Cites.* LY:296-310, LY:446, EM:723.
203	
204	**HE-26. Doors and the counterplay set.** *Rule.* A closed door leaf is solid to the horror (Layout `solid_in`). It issues no `set_opening`, opens no door, and may GOUGE or RUPTURE a hull segment, never a door. The **whole MVP counterplay set** is: retreat (walk away: `V_HUNT_MPX < V_WALK × 1000`), close a door (the strike room test and solid leaf; the horror holds at the sill and marks the leaf, below), go dark (the seat leaves target preference on the next run **only if no other light reaches it: a lamp-off seat under a lit fixture or in a Chemlight pool is still lit and still targetable, HE-13** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; its price is every lit-only channelled verb for the breach and the ship under STRESS unattended), pod-hop (the departed seat leaves `locus_body`, so `exogenous_permitted(actor_section(seat))` fails and an in-flight REACH on it fizzles; on a derelict locus, the departure of the last occupant recorded at BREACH entry also ends the breach, AT-12 (iii)), drop the cargo (turns a carrier into a walker) and the **glowstick work-light** (*light the job, not yourself*: a thrown Chemlight lights a workspace so the player can step out of it dark; it does not pull the horror). The suppressant is *not* in the set (HE-39). **A horror may path and stand in derelict A's `a_spine` at the MVP** (Boarding ASK-BS-H1 / OQ-BS-33 answered by the owner) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R21: the option that needs the least new content and preserves user rulings X6 and D63)*: ingress (HE-20) lands at a hull entry one room hop from the lit seat's room and never in a living seat's room, and a stalking horror follows the lit seat through any open door, so a carrier in the 3-wide spine can meet one. No bypass is added and the spine is not widened, because the ruled exits already hold in a single corridor: drop the cargo and walk back the way the carrier came (a walking seat outpaces `V_HUNT_MPX`, HE-24), stillness and darkness, or a door shut behind; this is the intended price of hauling (D63, 7 of 18 draws for a carrier who keeps the cargo, E-HE-27). The existing guards are the dead-end lint (E-HE-26) and the drop's one-free-cell question (Open Question 7); E-HE-59. **The anti-pillar's "tools may repel or distract (flares, torches, decoys)" is deliberately unused at MVP and deferred to Vertical Slice (`repel`, flares, decoys): MVP counterplay is avoidance only, and the routed thread's "tools repel, never kill" is a boundary (no tool ever kills, HE-38) and not an MVP promise that a tool repels.** *(orchestrator ruling: the earlier phrase "glowstick lure" is reworded because HE-13 prefers seats only and a glowstick is not a seat; creative-director concurs; decoys are Vertical Slice.)* No response is free and none is dominant: abort loses the job, hiding loses the task and the ship, going dark loses the lit verbs, committing risks a rung. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G2)* **A closed door is a priced, visible refuge** (the creative-director's lean, taken because the user delegated the call). When the target is a lit seat behind a closed or impassable leaf, the horror walks to the surrogate goal (HE-25) and **camps at the sill**: on the run it becomes stationary there (edge-triggered by the persisted `held_at_leaf` flag) it lays one HAIRLINES mark on the leaf face (a true ring entry; no M17 call, no hull damage, no GOUGE, no RUPTURE; counter `horror_leaf_marks`), and it stays while that seat remains the target and the phase is BREACH, recomputing the target every run as ever. The door therefore costs what the rules already price (the task, the ship under STRESS, the lit verbs while dark) and now also shows the player that the thing is waiting on the other side, with the leaf mark as the post-hoc evidence; what it does not do is damage the ship on the player's behalf. The alternatives (an anchor GOUGE fallback; leaving the playtest band as the only price) are recorded in Open Question 33 and not adopted. **A door closed on the horror.** If a leaf closes while the horror's foot box overlaps it (Layout's close-safety counts seats' foot boxes, not the horror's), the next run ejects it as the first step of guard 4: it moves back along `−last_octant` in 8 px increments up to 32 px to the first position for which `solid_in(foot_box)` is false (at most four queries, inside the five-query budget); if none is free it is wedged (RETREAT, `horror_wedged`, HE-25). It never embeds, wedges silently or passes through a leaf; counter `horror_door_ejected`; AC-HE-137. The preferred long-term fix, Layout's close-safety including a published horror foot box (`OBSTRUCTED`), is an ask in Open Question 32 and would make the eject unreachable. *Cites.* AT-12, DA-29, EM:89.

207	
208	**HE-27. Footprint taxonomy: two halves, both truth channel.** *Rule.* Horror's footprints split exactly as Failure & Trail splits them: M17 kinds surface only as Graph descriptors that F&T draws, and the web-grammar marks are Horror's own.

221	**STRUCK is the hit-only mark** (CD-GDD-ALIGN): the touch-down SMEAR is laid at the hold stage on a hit and on a miss alike (a REACH that fizzles earlier lays none), so STRUCK is what makes the floor differ after the two. It is a HAIRLINES-class mark for priority, protection from smear eviction, lifetime and ageing, and it is laid whether or not P is near a hull face (a hull contact adds its own HAIRLINES at the contact point, so a hit at a wall leaves both). Dust direction and filament twitch are Vertical Slice A: the dust process is the Attention Presenter's, and `web_strand_*`, `vfx_tell_*` and the band-slide are exclusive to it (AV-18, AC-AT-113). The Graph has no mark record, so a persisted Horror ring is the only way a reload cannot lie by omission (Pillar 1). *CHILL is bookkeeping, and this document says so:* at `CHILL_STEP_DJ` 3000 a mark cools a 20-tile room by 0.05 degC (`C_TILE` 3000, registry, LSG:458), below the Graph's own "invisible" row (LSG:912) and far below the COOL band; the rime on the floor is **a surface mark the web leaves, not a claim about air temperature**, and the physical deposit is route-choice and Debug Overlay bookkeeping. Claiming otherwise would be the hidden-stat shape Pillar 1 forbids. *(orchestrator ruling: option B of the CHILL magnitude question; dropping CHILL at MVP would also be acceptable and is the degrade path.)* *Cites.* FT:199, FT:1412, LSG:196, LSG:912, CON:243.
222	
223	**HE-28. Write path (a): published mutators, no commands.** *Rule.* `deposit_trace` (M17) and `apply_suit_damage` are **path (a)** of CR-9: published unconditional Class B mutators called from Horror's own P3 hook; the kernel names "a horror writing a footprint into the Graph's footprint channel" as the path-(a) example (KRN:104). Horror submits **no `SYSTEM`-origin command at MVP**, because no target of Horror's can reject. Attention's C22 and E-29 ("SYSTEM commands in P2") and LSG:807 ("the first 16 in arrival order within P2") carry a P2 premise that path (a) does not satisfy; this GDD **asserts no drain order** and lists both as owed refresh rows (C-HE-3). *Why.* The kernel is the authority on paths, and the budget rule of HE-29 holds under any drain order. *Cites.* KRN:104, AT:197, LSG:807.
224	
225	**HE-29. Per-window footprint budget and per-run cap.** *Rule.* Horror counts its accepted M17 calls per **Graph window**, defined as *the deposits the next `graph.propagate` run drains*: writes made at tick `T` in `[6k, 6k+5]` drain at the Graph run at `6(k+1)`, because `horror.step` runs after `graph.propagate.failure` on coinciding ticks (via `attention.step` and `emitter.place`) and so can never be drained by the run it follows (window index `w = floor(T / 6)`, the Graph's divisor 6, offset 0, LSG:104). Horror never exceeds `HE_FOOTPRINT_BUDGET = MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP − STRESS_DEPOSITS_PER_RUN` (16 − 8 = 8; DERIVED) per window, regardless of drain order. Because Horror's divisor (5) differs from the Graph's (6), one Graph window in five contains **two** Horror runs (`T mod 30` of 0 and 5, both inside `[6k, 6k+5]` for `k = 5j`); a per-run cap `MAX_DEPOSITS_PER_RUN` 4 keeps two runs at or under the window budget (`2 × MAX_DEPOSITS_PER_RUN <= HE_FOOTPRINT_BUDGET`). Priority inside a run: RUPTURE, then GOUGE, then CHILL. Writes over either bound are **not attempted** (a trace is "a moment, not a queue", LSG:807) and are counted `horror_footprints_withheld`; in nominal play that counter is a defect signal and never a gameplay state. Horror's 8-call window budget is the remainder of the registered global per-run cap (`MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP` 16, "deposit_trace writes honoured per run across all callers", LSG:807), so Horror leaves Attention's `STRESS_DEPOSITS_PER_RUN` whole. Natural worst case per run: one hull deposit (RUPTURE or GOUGE, one per STRIKE, HE-F17) and one CHILL = 2; the three-kind run of E-HE-13 is a stub fixture for the priority rule (priority RUPTURE, GOUGE, CHILL). *Cites.* AT:197, AC-AT-92, LSG:807, LSG:911, REG `MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP`.
226	
227	**HE-30. The mark ring.** *Rule.* The ring holds at most `MAX_MARKS` records `{mark_id, kind, section_id, pos_px, seed, life_left_ticks}` (`kind` in SMEAR, RIME, HAIRLINES, STRUCK); `mark_id` comes from an in-block counter and is never reused. `seed = he_hash(mark_id, 0, 0, SALT_MARK)` (HE-42), **never `rng_derive`** (the precedent of Lighting LO-19 and Attention AT-20). **Per-kind quotas** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: rime is protected from eviction and used to pile up through a long CALM LURK, and the strike, ingress and egress marks of a 3600-tick breach add up to eight more, so the unquota'd rule let `n_other` exceed the figure the smear-retention relation assumed. The ring holds at most `MARK_QUOTA_RIME` RIME marks (7), `MARK_QUOTA_HAIRLINES` HAIRLINES marks (3: strike, GOUGE, RUPTURE, anchor, ingress and egress contacts) and `MARK_QUOTA_STRUCK` STRUCK marks (3, one per landed strike), so `n_other_max = 13` (derived), and SMEAR has the rest of the ring, `MAX_MARKS − n_other_max >= 19` (HE-F7). Inserting a mark of a quota'd kind that is already at its quota evicts the **oldest mark of that kind** (lowest `mark_id`); inserting a SMEAR into a full ring evicts the oldest SMEAR, and a SMEAR is always resident in a full ring because `MAX_MARKS > n_other_max`. The STRUCK mark (at P) and the hull-contact HAIRLINES mark (at the contact point) are two marks of two kinds, each counted in its own quota; a hit beside a wall leaves both. The earlier fallback "evict the lowest `mark_id` of any kind when no SMEAR is resident" is unreachable and survives only as a defensive assertion (E-HE-8). `life_left_ticks` starts at `MARK_LIFE_TICKS` and falls by 5 per run while the mark's section is loaded; the mark is removed at zero. A SMEAR is laid per `MARK_SPACING_PX` of moved distance while the record moves and one touch-down SMEAR at P at each REACH's hold stage (a stationary horror lays nothing else, so a long LURK does not flush the ring), a RIME at each CHILL deposit, HAIRLINES at hull contact (HE-16) and at ingress and egress, and one STRUCK at P on a STRIKE that called `apply_suit_damage` (HE-15). At most `MARKS_PER_RUN_MAX` inserts per run, in the priority STRUCK, HAIRLINES, RIME, SMEAR (a hit's record is never the insert that is dropped). Marks are laid whenever the entity moves or acts, **regardless of any viewer's hallucination state** (HE-32), and are drawn by a Horror PRESENTATION subscriber in the floor-marks band within `HORROR_MARK_DRAW_GROUPS` of the shared `D_marks` budget (Failure & Trail's `TRAIL_DMARKS_SHARE` 6 of `D_marks` 4-20 "crowds Horror's footprints out", FT:816). Every mutation marks its dirty keys **explicitly**: in Godot 4.7 packed-array element writes do not call the setter, a HIGH silent-failure class (breaking-changes, CR-8). *(orchestrator ruling: checkpoint CP-5; C-HE-12 closed. A long creep can no longer evict the hairlines of a strike while any smear remains.)* *Why.* Option B of the footprint taxonomy: the sim stays the authority and the view is reconstructible after a load. *Cites.* PIPE:137, PIPE:616, FT:816.
228	
229	**HE-31. Rime and mark honesty.** *Rule.* Rime is **hue-less**, rendered L\* 70 to 78, with **non-repeating** branch angles taken from the mark's `seed`, and **never at a coolant fitting**: a CHILL deposit and its rime mark are withheld when the deposit point is within `FITTING_CLEARANCE_PX` of a coolant-loop fitting node (counter `horror_chill_withheld_fitting`), so a fitting never shows Horror rime. No flesh (hue 5-30, S 20-60 %, V 45-85 %), no violet (hue 270-330, S above 25 %), no Alarm Red, Chemlight or Tungsten appears in any mark (FT:886). A runtime guard withholds a CHILL deposit that would bring a compartment closer to `COLD_DMG_ONSET_MC` than `CHILL_MARGIN_MC`, and the data lint bounds the cumulative CHILL per compartment per epoch (HE-F4): **the cold of passage is a footprint, never a killer.** The AC-79 collision fixtures (frost fan against branching rime; RUPTURE trail against footprint) are blind-classified and signed off by the art-director. The art-director's proposed palette entry is **Rime White-Grey `#B0B8C0` `[PROVISIONAL]`**; the entry itself is an art-bible decision (creative-director, art-director), and until it lands the rime has no palette candidate (C-HE-21 open; it blocks asset-spec for rime and hairlines, not this GDD). *Cites.* FT:1427, FT:886, FT:1032, REG `COLD_DMG_ONSET_MC`.
230	
231	**HE-32. Footprints survive hallucination.** *Rule.* A real entity, registered under HE-34, keeps depositing M17 writes, marks, disturbance state and suit damage **whether or not any seat's Filter hides its body**; these outputs are bit-identical with and without a Filter stub (CON:243: "the hallucination hides the body, never the trail"). Horror holds no sanity reference and reads no `PERCEPTION_OUT` block (H5, CR-12). Phantom horrors are the Filter's: no Body row, no footprint, no M17 call, no record in `horror.state`, no registration with the Emitter, and Sanity's own rule matches (a phantom "exists only in `sanity.perception`", never registered, no footprint). A HIDE entry names a real HORROR ref; the entity stays registered and keeps obeying AT-15. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: Sanity & Hallucination Rules and the Perception Filter are both `Status: Designed` and repeat this; Filter truth-table row 7 and SN-22.)* *Cites.* CON:243, SN-22, H5.
232	
233	**HE-33. Seat reads.** *Rule.* Horror enumerates the seats on a body with Body's `actors_on(body_id)`, reads each seat's `pos_curr(actor_id)` and `actor_section(actor_id)` (Body's SIM read view, BDY-29, BDY-30), and reads the seat's life state (`DOWNED`, `DEAD`, `IN_POD`, `STAGGERED`) from the Controller's `controller.state` `loco_state`, which Suit states is readable (SE:333; the published read is `controller.state.loco_state` through the `SIM` read view, PCI:58 and :241, C-HE-18 closed) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. The mapping from actor to `player_id` for `apply_suit_damage` is Body's and the Controller's binding *(provisional — read name owed)*. Horror reads **no** suit integrity value and no Suit rung (it never needs one: the rung ladder is Suit's); it reads no Sanity value and no `PERCEPTION_OUT` block. The predicate argument is always Body's `actor_section`, not the Graph's `section_of`. *Cites.* BDY-29, SE:333, PCI-14.
234	
235	#### Group G — Light
236	
237	**HE-34. Emitter subjects.** *Rule.* Each non-TRANSIT record is an Emitter HORROR subject: E6 `register_subject(ref, HORROR, anchor_px, section_id)` at arrival, E8 `set_subject_anchor(ref, anchor_px)` once per run (the E6/E8 anchor is in the record's current body frame, as re-based by HE-22 after a weld or cut *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; E8 is called once per run and lands at the next `emitter.place`: the one-tick lag EM:154 accepts. The anchor is otherwise current, because the sim position changes only at runs (HE-23)), E7 `unregister_subject(ref)` at egress or unload; registrations are canonical in `emitter.state` and survive a restore (EM-28, EM:712); in its own `post_restore` the record calls E6 only when it is non-TRANSIT and its ref is absent from the Emitter subject table; a duplicate E6 returns false by design (EM:152) and is not a defect. HORROR is always `moving` (EM-21). An unregistered ref answers like an unlit one (`lux` 0, `lit` false). A false return from E6 on a first registration (the `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS` overflow, `emitter_subjects_overflow` increments, EM AC-27) is a **budget defect** (the subject reads dark) and a lint or acceptance-criterion failure, never a gameplay state; a false return on an already-registered ref is not. Horror reads `lux(ref)` only (its lit test is the stateless `lux_pm >= LIT_ON_PM` of HE-13, not the Emitter's `lit` bit) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; it calls no `probe` at MVP (Emitter EM-24 anticipates Horror pathing probes; HE-25 pathing needs none, so Horror consumes none of `MAX_PROBES_PER_TICK` 4, shared with Interaction (Attention makes no `probe()` call and does not read it, AT-4), and "Horror spams probes: only `probes_allowed` are served", EM:723). `HORROR_SUBJECTS_MAX` 2 (one active plus one transient during ingress), range 1 to 12; the Emitter's "placeholder 12" (EM:229) is a ceiling Horror owns, not the plan; I-CAPS (d) holds (2 + actors 4 ≤ `MAX_MOVING_SUBJECTS` 16). Interaction's `H` (REG `subject_budget`) and Derelict Authoring's `HORRORS` now quote this registered number, `HORROR_SUBJECTS_MAX` 2 (C-HE-4, closed 2026-10-27). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **One registration rule, for body load and `post_restore` alike:** a record is an Emitter subject iff it is non-TRANSIT and its body is loaded. On every run, after guard 2 and before guard 3, the record reconciles: body loaded, non-TRANSIT and its ref absent from the Emitter subject table, then E6 at its stored `pos_px` (this is the first run after a body loads, including first boarding, and the first run after a restore, so a resident LURK in derelict B reads lit the moment the player boards, which the CALM-sighting goal needs); body unloaded and the ref still registered, then E7 once. Both calls are idempotent through the table read, and neither is a step: an unloaded record performs no other act (HE-21). AC-HE-140. *Cites.* EM-21, EM-24, EM:229.
238	
239	**HE-35. L3 light disturbance: published state, never a call.** *Rule.* `horror.view.disturbances[]` lists `{emitter_id, strength_pm, start_T, dur_ticks}` for emitters of kind FIXTURE and NODE_LANTERN in the horror's body within `L3_RADIUS_PX` of its foot point, in **any phase**. **Never** a BEAM, a BEACON, a FAULT_GLOW, any DEPLOYABLE (glowsticks), and **never the EMERGENCY fixture subkind** (`fx_cryo_lamp`) **and never the DOCK_STATUS fixture subkind** (a dock room's self-powered pod status glow, Emitter EM-3: a SYSTEM-switched status light is not a disturbance carrier, since a dip on it would read as a false tell; Lighting LO-20, Attention AT-20) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6; Lighting LO-20 now exempts DOCK_STATUS per Attention AT-20 / user ruling X2)*: this is Horror's answer to Lighting's open questions 15 and 22, "EMERGENCY stays exempt" (and, from 2026-10-28, DOCK_STATUS with it). A disturbance starts on an eligible lamp at a run when `he_hash(emitter_id, run_n, 0, SALT_L3_START) mod 1000 < L3_START_PM` (HE-42) and `T >= last_end_T + L3_MIN_GAP_TICKS` (the ruled `L3_MIN_GAP_FRAMES` 120 is stored in ticks because a SIM block cannot count presentation frames, H9; one tick equals one frame at the nominal 60 fps and Lighting maps it). `strength_pm` lies in `[L3_STRENGTH_LO_PM, 1000 − MOD_FLOOR_PM]` and `dur_ticks` in `[L3_DUR_LO, L3_DUR_HI]`, both from `he_hash` with their own salts (`SALT_L3_STRENGTH`, `SALT_L3_DUR`; HE-F11); at most `L3_MAX_ACTIVE` lamps at once. A disturbance changes a lamp's **output only**: no disturbance touches a beam, the beacon, a fault glow or a glowstick, or changes a real light's radius, position or colour (Lighting's submitter contract, LO OQ 15). Horror never writes an Emitter field, never feeds the query and never calls Lighting (KRN:117; LO:424 must-repeat verbatim: disturbance is never applied to a BEAM, BEACON, FAULT_GLOW or any DEPLOYABLE, never an Emitter field, never an input to the query; horrors never occlude and emit nothing). The verb "flicker" never describes a fixture (LO-20). Disturbances are persisted (save-equivalence). The lamp enumeration near a point is the Emitter's `emitters_near(body_id, px, r)` (ids of emitters on the body whose origin lies within `r` px, ascending id; a filter of the records, not a probe; Emitter read table): Horror filters the returned ids to FIXTURE and NODE_LANTERN (excluding the EMERGENCY and DOCK_STATUS subkinds) from the emitter records, so an exempt lamp never takes an `L3_MAX_ACTIVE` slot or a `last_end_T` entry *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; C-HE-15 is closed 2026-10-27 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; was provisional)*. *Why.* The Pillar 4(a) "light disturbance" footprint: local and unsynchronised, which separates it from the tell (global, beat-locked, AT:1184); the player's test is "is it everywhere on the beat, or one place?". *Cites.* LO-18, LO-19, LO-20, LO:424, LO OQ 15 and 22, EM-3, AT-20.
240	
241	**HE-36. No noise push.** *Rule.* Horror calls `push_stimulus` **never**. Audio facts stay published (HE-37). *Why.* A horror that feeds the ledger can hold BREACH open past `CLEAR_HOLD_TICKS` (the C8 spiral) and puts a lever outside the player's restraint (Pillar 3). AC-AT-95 refuses any `push_stimulus` caller other than the Controller and Interaction (a Horror double is refused), so Horror is not a declared caller (registry `push_stimulus`). *Cites.* AT:373, AC-AT-95.
242	
243	#### Group H — Information, rules and reward
244	
245	**HE-37. Audio and presentation facts, not sounds.** *Rule.* `horror.view` publishes, per entity: `entity_id`, `type_id`, `state` (LURK, STALK, REACH, STRIKE, RETREAT, TRANSIT), `pos_px`, `body_id`, `section_id`, `locked_pt` and `reach_end_T` (REACH), `strike_T` and the seats hit (STRIKE), `transit_until_T`, ingress and egress events with their tick, `disturbances[]`, the mark ring, and diagnostic counters (`horror_footprints_withheld`, `horror_marks_withheld`, `horror_ingress_pending`, `horror_chill_withheld_*`, E6 refusals). These `horror_*` names are **frozen** for the Debug Overlay, which reads them by channel and restates none as a fact (DO P-11). Adaptive Audio owns every sound, mix and cue name; the Horror sub-tell family is **disjoint** from Attention's tell family, the Graph loop sounds and Sanity's hallucination family (Audio AA-6 (the identity table), Sanity R28); phantom horrors use the Filter and Sanity audio classes, **never the Graph witness acoustic classes**. Horror never mutes, ducks or filters anything. A `tell_id` and `type_id` enumeration is kept stable and enumerable so the Knowledge Codex (Vertical Slice) can target one. Designed (`adaptive-audio-and-tells.md`, AA-28, AA-29). *Cites.* AT:1204, IDX:41.
246	
247	**HE-38. No combat, no reward.** *Rule.* No horror HP, no kill state, no loot, no XP, no kill counter, no hit feedback for tool use, no player damage output, no hit-stop, no screen shake, no damage number, no threat bar and no proximity indicator. HORROR subjects take no verb at MVP: any forced command is `INVALID_TARGET` (IA-39, AC-IA-113). The beam only reveals (HE-13). "HORROR subjects take no verb" holds at MVP only; the Vertical Slice B `repel` declaration fields and their parity precondition (IA-31) are recorded in Open Questions row 27 only. The data-file lint of HE-5 and a repository scan for the feedback words in the vocabulary list are acceptance criteria. *Why.* The anti-pillar "not a combat game"; "horrors are avoided and survived, not farmed". *Cites.* IA:288, IA:468, PC-12, FT:98.
248	
249	**HE-39. Suppressant: a data-dormant interface; `tool_suppressant` is out of the MVP start kit.** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *Rule.* **No suppressant effect ships at MVP**, per AT-19 (designed, CD-approved: "no effect verb ships at MVP ... a Vertical Slice addendum"; a suppressant that aborts a tell would "make restraint an item"). Horror declares only the dormant interface `repel(origin, T)` with `REPEL_RADIUS_PX` 192 and `REPEL_TICKS` 600 [PLACEHOLDER]: any record within the radius would go RETREAT for the window, begin no REACH or STRIKE, never die, drop nothing, never touch Attention's level or tell. When the effect verb ships, its registrant reads the suppressant's `OUT_OF_CHARGES` through Suit's `tool_charge(player_id, def_id)` (SE read table); Horror never stores or writes a charge. Its acceptance criteria read **NOT ASSESSED at MVP, never PASS**. **Conflict C-HE-6 — closed. Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): Option A (X6).** The start kit carried `tool_suppressant` with `SUPPRESSANT_START_CHARGES` 3 and no effect, a Pillar 1 problem of its own (a tool whose use changes nothing in the world is a lie the sane game tells). `tool_suppressant` is removed from the MVP start kit (SE-11 slot 4, SE-14, SE-15), from the Item DB MVP list and from the HUD, and returns with its effect verb at Vertical Slice; the registry name `SUPPRESSANT_START_CHARGES` is retired (status deprecated). HE-39 keeps the dormant `repel` interface, marked **`[CUT-FIRST]`**: if AT-19 is reversed at Vertical Slice the effect and the item arrive together and it is a one-owner change. **Gate:** AC-HE-124 is BLOCKING; Item DB AC-109 (the start kit has no consumer-less def) passes. The edits to Suit, the Item DB, the HUD and Attention are those owners' (Open Question 3); then the consistency check is rerun. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *Cites.* AT:243, SE:201, IDB:249.
250	
251	**HE-40. Rig presenter, Sanity and the Perception Filter.** *Rule.* A render-side rig presenter takes `(pose_stream, type_id)` and an optional `leak` input that **only the Filter may set**; Horror feeds it real poses with `leak` 0; the Filter (Vertical Slice) may feed phantom or crewmate-driven poses (ART:594 "0 extra frames"; class (c) is driven by the crewmate's true velocity and true beam). Conformance to the Pipeline's row 14: Y-sort with the core's foot row as sort origin, 15-degree quantised segment rotation, pose stepped every 5th tick, `present_time` is not the rig's clock (PR-9), the presenter derives a five-tick interpolation alpha from the kernel's one-tick `tick_alpha` (owed to the Pipeline, C-HE-14), and horror presentation never writes the camera (C1, C9; the jolt API refuses it). Three canonical poses (rest, reach, move) pass the silhouette test: no closed circle, no bilateral symmetry, no four-limb pairs, no emission, iridescence band only under light. A rig instance with no Horror ref in `horror.view` and `leak` 0 is a lint error. Sanity's rulings decide what Horror owes: keep every real entity registered (E6) with a true anchor and publish true positions in `horror.view`; Horror computes no exposure, owns neither `HORROR_NEAR_R` (called `HORROR_SEEN_R` in the Sanity rulings; renamed in the Sanity draft, C-HE-32) nor `EXP_HORROR`, and holds no sanity reference. -> ADR candidate (3). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: Sanity and the Perception Filter are both `Status: Designed`.)* *Cites.* PIPE:303, PCI row 16, ART:594, SN-22.

284	### States and Transitions
285	
286	The record's `state` takes one of six values: `LURK`, `STALK`, `REACH`, `STRIKE`, `RETREAT`, `TRANSIT`. The first five are the cycle; `TRANSIT` is a **sixth value, additive** to the five the audio facts need (C-HE-17): relocation through a hull needs a visible place in the machine and has no position. "Permitted act" is what the state may do to the world. Dormancy (HE-21) is not a state: a record whose body is unloaded is frozen in whatever state it holds, with no step.
287	
288	#### State table
289	
290	| State | Entry (from, guard) | Phases it lives in | Permitted act | Registered subject | Motion | Exit (first match wins) | Who may cause the transition |
291	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
292	| **LURK** | boot or default; STALK on a TELL abort; RETREAT when the phase is CALM or TELL and the record is not returning; TRANSIT arrival while the phase is CALM | CALM (any other phase only transiently) | marks, CHILL, disturbance dips; no RUPTURE, no GOUGE, no suit damage; never within `LURK_STANDOFF_PX` of a living seat | yes | `V_CREEP_MPX` between waypoints; dwell `LURK_DWELL_TICKS` | `attention.view.phase` = TELL with a new `tell_epoch` → STALK (locus body is its body) or TRANSIT (another body; evaluated first, so it fires even when the record's own body is unloaded); return due → TRANSIT; body unloaded and the locus body is its own or none → frozen *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | **Attention's phase only** (HE-7); never the player's light, noise or distance |
293	| **STALK** | LURK on TELL entry; RETREAT when the cooldown has elapsed in BREACH; TRANSIT arrival in TELL or BREACH | TELL, BREACH | marks, CHILL, disturbance. TELL: the standoff holds, no harm. BREACH: may begin a REACH under HE-14 | yes | TELL `V_CREEP_MPX`; BREACH `V_HUNT_MPX` | TELL abort (phase back to CALM) → LURK; BREACH and HE-14 (a) to (f) true → REACH; SUBSIDING → RETREAT; no lit seat → the anchor becomes the target (still STALK) | `attention.view` fields and the stateless `lux_pm >= LIT_ON_PM` read of HE-13 (not the Emitter's `lit` bit); the abort is Attention's *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
294	| **REACH** | STALK in BREACH when the predicate holds at begin | BREACH (resolves in BREACH or SUBSIDING) | lays the touch-down SMEAR at P at the start of the hold stage (a pre-hold fizzle lays none, HE-14); publishes `reach_start_T`, `locked_pt` and `reach_end_T`; no harm yet; rooted | yes | none | `T >= reach_end_T` and the predicate holds → STRIKE; the predicate false at that run, or the phase CALM, or a restore with the predicate false → RETREAT (fizzle: no harm, no hairlines, no GOUGE or RUPTURE, no cooldown; an already-laid touch-down smear stays); `SUBSIDE_CANCELS_REACH` 1 and SUBSIDING → RETREAT (fizzle) | the predicate (Attention's `exogenous_permitted`); the horror's own clock |
295	| **STRIKE** | REACH resolve | BREACH or SUBSIDING | on the entry run only: `apply_suit_damage` per HE-15; GOUGE and RUPTURE per HE-16; hairline mark; publishes `strike_T` and the seats hit | yes | none (the snap pose) | after `STRIKE_HOLD_RUNS` runs → RETREAT | the horror's own clock |
296	| **RETREAT** | STRIKE; a fizzle; SUBSIDING entry; (Vertical Slice) a `repel` | BREACH, SUBSIDING, then CALM | marks only | yes | `V_CREEP_MPX` away from every living seat | `T >= cooldown_until_T` and BREACH → STALK; CALM or TELL and not returning → LURK; return due → TRANSIT | Attention's phase; the horror's own clock |
297	| **TRANSIT** | TELL entry with `body_of(locus_section_id)` not its own (also from an unloaded body, HE-20); return due (`RETURN_DELAY_TICKS`); its section lost to a cut (HE-22) | any | none; no position, no marks (the egress and ingress marks are laid at the segments, not by the traveller), not registered | no | none | `T >= transit_until_T` and a legal entry (HE-20) → STALK (TELL or BREACH), LURK (CALM) or RETREAT (SUBSIDING), with E6 and an ingress mark; a TELL abort while outbound cancels the arrival and retargets to `from_body_id` (HE-20); a new `tell_epoch` retargets to the new locus body *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | Attention's locus; Layout for legality |
298	
299	#### Phase view (state against phase: the single table a reviewer tests against)
300	
301	| Phase | LURK | STALK | REACH | STRIKE | RETREAT | TRANSIT |
302	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
303	| CALM | resident | → LURK (after an abort) | fizzle | n/a | → LURK | an abort cancels an outbound arrival (the record heads back; it never arrives as LURK from an abort) |
304	| TELL | → STALK | creep, standoff holds, no harm | cannot begin | n/a | → LURK | arrives as STALK |
305	| BREACH | n/a | hunt; may begin a REACH | the telegraph | harm (predicate) | cooldown | arrives as STALK |
306	| SUBSIDING | n/a | → RETREAT | resolves or fizzles | harm only if resolving | stays | arrives as RETREAT |
307	
308	*(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the CALM/TRANSIT cell no longer reads "arrives as LURK" after an abort, HE-20; a TRANSIT record that reached its arrival run in CALM for any other reason, such as a return home completing, still arrives as LURK.)*
309	
310	A TELL abort moves the phase from TELL to CALM; the record in STALK returns to LURK with no strike and no mark burst (HE-12). A record in RETREAT during a second TELL goes RETREAT → LURK → STALK on the new `tell_epoch`; it never skips LURK. Predicate check points (each is an acceptance criterion): REACH begin (HE-14 c), STRIKE entry (HE-15), every M17 RUPTURE or GOUGE call (HE-16, HE-29). All three read `exogenous_permitted` at their own tick. CHILL is a non-harm footprint, permitted in any phase, bounded by HE-F4 and HE-31 (C-HE-28).
311	
312	#### Transition guards (ordered; the first match wins within a run)
313	
314	1. **Restore-first.** A run that follows a restore re-checks the predicate for any record in REACH (HE-41) before any other guard.
315	2. **Tell edge (new `tell_epoch`; runs for every record in every run, ahead of dormancy)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; was guard 4, which sat behind dormancy so a record whose body was unloaded never saw the edge)*. If `tell_epoch != last_seen_tell_epoch`: zero the five epoch counters and empty `gouged_seg_ids`, set `last_seen_tell_epoch := tell_epoch`, and take a record in REACH to a fizzle (HE-17: no harm, no cooldown consumed) and a record in STRIKE out of its hold, each going to RETREAT in this run (a new `tell_epoch` means the previous breach is over) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; then LURK → STALK (the locus body is the record's body; a record found in RETREAT or STALK passes through LURK first, never skipping it, E-HE-16) or LURK / STALK / RETREAT → TRANSIT (another body; a departure from an unloaded body is allowed, HE-20, and is the only act an unloaded record performs); a record already in TRANSIT retargets to the new locus body (HE-20). Nothing else in the run may act on the record before this check.
316	3. **Dormancy** *(after the registration reconciliation of HE-34, which runs between guards 2 and 3)*. The record's body is not loaded and the record is not in TRANSIT → no step (HE-21). (A TRANSIT record has no body; its wait for an unloaded destination is HE-21's second rule.)
317	4. **Layout change.** `layout.state` changed since the last run, or `version(section_id)` changed for a section of the record's body (a door opened or closed) → first the door-eject check of HE-26 (a leaf closed on the horror's foot box), then invalidate the path cache and re-derive `body_id` from `body_of(section_id)` (HE-22) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
318	5. **Phase edge (the rest).** The phase returned to CALM from TELL (an abort) → STALK → LURK, or an outbound TRANSIT (`transit_leg` OUTBOUND) is cancelled and retargeted to `from_body_id` with `transit_leg` RETURN (HE-20); SUBSIDING → STALK → RETREAT. A record in REACH or STRIKE is untouched by this guard (guard 6 resolves it).
319	6. **Cycle guards** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. **Independent of phase:** REACH → STRIKE or fizzle at `T >= reach_end_T` (a REACH begun in BREACH resolves in SUBSIDING, HE-17, and fizzles in CALM or when `SUBSIDE_CANCELS_REACH` is 1) and STRIKE → RETREAT after `STRIKE_HOLD_RUNS`. **In BREACH only:** STALK → REACH (HE-14) and RETREAT → STALK.
320	7. **Return.** `RETURN_DELAY_TICKS` after the end of SUBSIDING or a TELL abort and not in the home body → TRANSIT.
321	
322	**Epoch counters.** `strikes_epoch`, `gouges_epoch`, `ruptures_epoch`, `chill_epoch_dj` and `chill_deposits_epoch` reset **lazily, keyed on the comparison `tell_epoch != last_seen_tell_epoch` and not on observing the phase edge itself**: at the first run in which a record sees that inequality (guard 2, which runs first), the five counters are zeroed, `gouged_seg_ids` is emptied and `last_seen_tell_epoch` is updated before any act in that run. A record that slept through one or more TELLs, or a save restored from an older epoch, therefore wakes with zero counters and its caps bind correctly. Caps bound each told epoch, and CALM activity after a breach counts against that epoch's remaining allowance until the next TELL. `epoch_id` (HE-41) is set to the new `tell_epoch` at the same moment *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
323	
324	#### Published fields by state (`horror.view`)
325	
326	| State | Published beyond the always-present `entity_id`, `type_id`, `state`, `body_id`, `section_id`, `pos_px` |
327	|---|---|
328	| LURK, STALK, RETREAT | `state_enter_T`; the disturbance list; diagnostic counters |
329	| REACH | `reach_start_T`, `locked_pt`, `reach_end_T` (the rig and Audio read them; the player reads the limb; `reach_start_T` keeps replay and TellAudit able to see when the REACH began although the smear is laid later) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
330	| STRIKE | `strike_T`, the seats hit, the hull segments gouged or ruptured, the `tell_epoch` it ran in (TellAudit) |
331	| TRANSIT | `transit_until_T`, `transit_leg`, the pending ingress segment once chosen; no `pos_px` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
332	
333	#### Persisted timers and counters (all in `horror.state`; see HE-41)
334	
335	All fields of HE-41, and nothing else. The timers: `state_enter_T`, `reach_start_T`, `reach_end_T`, `cooldown_until_T`, `transit_until_T`, `ingress_mark_T`, `dwell_start_T`, `strike_T` and `last_seen_tell_epoch`. The counters: the `"horror.tell"` counter, `fp_count` for `fp_window`, the per-epoch ledgers (`strikes_epoch`, `gouges_epoch`, `ruptures_epoch`, `chill_epoch_dj`, `chill_deposits_epoch`, `gouged_seg_ids`), `hold_runs`, `blocked_runs`, `goal_commit_runs`, `smear_travel_px`, `chill_travel_px`, `lurk_dwell_index` and the `mark_id` counter. The mark ring with each mark's `life_left_ticks`, and the disturbance list with `last_end_T`. A restore reconstructs every state from these, never from the previous process's memory (G4 save-equivalence, given the pair (save, `restore_epoch`)); the committed field manifest (AC-HE-76) is the check that this list and HE-41 stay one list *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
336	
337	#### Cycle timing at the placeholders
338	
339	Minimum interval between two strike resolutions for a seat that has not moved is `STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS + UNFOLD_LO` = 395 ticks (6.6 s) when the horror is already in reach range. `UNFOLD_TICKS` is `5 × rng_int(19, 36)`: 18 equally likely values from 95 to 180 with mean 137.5, so the mean interval is 437.5 ticks (7.3 s) and the longest is 480 ticks (8.0 s). That is a lower bound: after a strike the horror retreats (96 ticks out at `V_CREEP_MPX`, inside the cooldown), turns at `cooldown_until_T` and walks back at `V_HUNT_MPX` (64 ticks, 65 on the run grid), so the realised period of a seat that does not move is `UNFOLD_TICKS + STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS + 65` = 460 to 545 ticks (7.7 to 9.1 s), mean 502.5 (registered formula HE-F15). The time to a third strike for a seat that never moves, and the share of minimum-length breaches that contain a third REACH start (none), are derived in HE-F16 and are not carried here.
340	
341	### Interactions with Other Systems
342	
343	Reading guide. "Neighbour's own row" quotes the dependency GDD's text about Horror Entities verbatim (columns of a quoted table row are separated by ` ‖ `), so that bidirectional consistency can be read in one place. "Path" is the kernel's CR-9 path: (a) a published unconditional mutator called from the caller's own hook, (b) a `SYSTEM`-origin command processed at T+1 when the target may reject. **Horror uses path (a) only and submits no `SYSTEM` command at MVP.** "Class A / Class B" is the mutator class (Class B clamps, never rejects). "Status" is the neighbour's state at authoring time. Rows for undesigned neighbours list **supplies and assumptions only** and are `[PROVISIONAL]`, each registered with the owner named.

829	## Edge Cases
830	
831	Each case states the exact outcome and the rule it follows. Ids are `E-HE-n`. "Fizzle" always means the HE-17 outcome: RETREAT with no harm, no hairlines, no GOUGE or RUPTURE and no cooldown consumed, an already-laid touch-down smear stays (a fizzle before the hold stage lays none), the `"horror.tell"` draw stays consumed. Where a case settles something the Detailed Design left silent, it is marked *(orchestrator ruling)* and is repeated in the review questions. Cases that depend on an undesigned neighbour are marked *(provisional — <dep>)*.
832	
833	#### Zero, maximum and out-of-range values
834	
835	- **If a seat stands at exactly `R_SNAP_PX` (72 px) from P at resolution (E-HE-1)**: it is not hit. The disc is strict, `dx² + dy² < R_SNAP_PX²` with integers (`5184 < 5184` is false). The walk-out arithmetic of HE-F5 depends on the strictness, and an integer comparison keeps the outcome identical on replay.
836	- **If a seat that is already CRITICAL (integrity 3600) is struck (E-HE-2)**: `I = max(0, 3600 − 3200) = 400`, below `SUIT_HP_FAIL`, so FAILED → DOWNED → `DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS` → DEAD on Suit's ladder. The horror enters RETREAT after the hold. With no living, non-DOWNED candidate left, the target is the anchor (HE-13, HE-F8). At `cooldown_until_T` in BREACH it STALKs toward the anchor and runs anchor REACHes (hairlines and at most one GOUGE under `GOUGES_PER_EPOCH_MAX`, never RUPTURE or `apply_suit_damage`, HE-16 (3)) until SUBSIDING sends it to RETREAT. It never LURKs in BREACH (phase view). The ladder and the death are Suit's, the restore is Save/Load's (HE-18).
837	- **If `apply_suit_damage` would take integrity below 0 (a patched suit at 2800 struck again) (E-HE-3)**: integrity clamps at 0 (`I_k = max(0, …)`, HE-F3); the mutator is Class B, clamp-never-reject, so Horror never sees a rejection and has no error path to write.
838	- **If the type row has `UNFOLD_LO` or `UNFOLD_HI` that is not a multiple of 5, `UNFOLD_HI < UNFOLD_LO`, or `UNFOLD_LO` below the HE-F5 bound (E-HE-4)**: the data load fails with a lint error and the type row is refused; nothing rounds silently. A silent round-up would bias every telegraph by 1 to 4 ticks at the exact bound that sizes the walk-out.
839	- **If `STRIKE_BP` is outside 3001..3500, `SUIT_PATCH_CAP_BP − STRIKE_BP` is below `SUIT_HP_FAIL`, or `STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS` is at or below `STAGGER_TICKS` (E-HE-5)**: the data load fails the registered bounds (HE-F3, the third being the one-strike-never-kills-a-patched-suit bound) or the cooldown invariant (HE-F15) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. A value outside the interval changes the hits-to-FAILED count, which is Suit's rung design, not Horror's to retune.
840	- **If a seat walks into the horror's mouth during a BREACH and the lit seat is already within `REACH_RANGE_PX` at the run the cooldown is clear (E-HE-6)**: the REACH begins on that run (conditions (a) to (f) of HE-14 hold); the telegraph is still at least `UNFOLD_LO` ticks and P is the seat's foot point at lock. A close approach shortens the horror's walk, never its warning.
841	- **If no waypoint is at least `LURK_STANDOFF_PX` from every living seat (a small body, seats on all sides) (E-HE-7)**: the horror holds its position and does nothing (the cornered rule of HE-11); it deposits no harm and lays no marks while still. A cornered horror is a stationary hazard, never a pursuer.
842	- **If a ring insert finds no SMEAR to evict (E-HE-8)**: unreachable by construction, because the per-kind quotas (HE-30) leave at least `MAX_MARKS − n_other_max` = 19 ring slots to SMEAR; a fixture that forces it fires the defensive assertion, which evicts the lowest `mark_id` of any kind and increments `horror_ring_invariant`, a defect signal and never a gameplay state *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
843	- **If more than `MARKS_PER_RUN_MAX` marks would be inserted in one run (E-HE-9)**: the first `MARKS_PER_RUN_MAX` are inserted in the order STRUCK, HAIRLINES, RIME, SMEAR and the rest are dropped and counted `horror_marks_withheld`. A run can legitimately want three (an ingress with smear, rime and hairlines); the cap bounds the dirty keys per tick (`MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256).
844	
845	#### Simultaneous rules
846	
847	- **If the predicate flips false between REACH begin and REACH end (the seat pod-hops, the breach is cleared early, the phase returns to CALM) (E-HE-10)**: the REACH fizzles at its last tick. The tip rested on P for the whole telegraph, a touch-down smear laid at the hold stage is a true mark and stays (a fizzle before the hold stage laid none), and the cooldown is not consumed, so a fizzle cannot starve the next legitimate REACH (HE-17).
848	- **If `reach_end_T` falls in SUBSIDING and the seat's section is still in `locus_body` (E-HE-11)**: the REACH resolves; the predicate holds in SUBSIDING for sections in `locus_body`, so `tell_window_contract` passes; the state then goes RETREAT. With `SUBSIDE_CANCELS_REACH` 1 it fizzles instead (the merciful variant, off by default; C-HE-10).
849	- **If a STRIKE is eligible for both GOUGE and RUPTURE on the same segment (E-HE-12)**: one hull deposit per STRIKE; RUPTURE when `rupture_ok` (which now requires an empty hit list), else GOUGE (HE-F17). The scrape (GOUGE) is always a separate, earlier, told act than the tear *(orchestrator ruling: HE-16 is silent on the tie)*.
850	- **If a REACH resolves on a seat that is already CRITICAL and staggered, beside a gouged hull face (E-HE-56)**: the seat is in the disc, so the hit list is not empty, `rupture_ok` is false and the deposit is a GOUGE (or none, if `GOUGES_PER_EPOCH_MAX` is spent); the strike's `apply_suit_damage` takes the seat from 3600 to 400 and FAILED as in E-HE-2, and no breach opens beside the dying seat. The compound "CRITICAL, staggered, plus a hull rupture" is excluded by construction. If the same seat is outside the disc, a RUPTURE may be issued and the Graph raises its own told breach clock (RUPTURE sets the segment to `RUPTURE_HP` 3600: decompression takes about 131 s at the initial hole, LSG:707), which a CRITICAL walk-only seat (`V_WALK` 2, about 15 000 px in that time) can outwalk or patch; AC-HE-133 asserts both halves *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. The miss-only RUPTURE rule is a user ruling (Open Question 2) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
851	- **If one run wants a RUPTURE, a GOUGE and a CHILL while the window already holds 6 accepted calls (E-HE-13)**: the priority RUPTURE, GOUGE, CHILL applies within `MAX_DEPOSITS_PER_RUN`, then the window budget of 8 binds; RUPTURE and GOUGE are issued (window total 8), the CHILL is withheld (its rime mark is still laid) and `horror_footprints_withheld` increments. Harm outranks bookkeeping.
852	- **If a weld or cut changes the layout on the same tick a REACH resolves (E-HE-14)**: the locked P stays the stored integer; the same-room test (HE-15) and the closed-leaf test (HE-19) are re-evaluated against the layout as it is at resolution. A seat whose room now differs from P's room is not hit, so a layout change can only spare a seat, never reach one through a new wall.
853	- **If TELL ends in an abort on the same run a TRANSIT arrival completes, or at any earlier run while the record is outbound (E-HE-15)**: the abort is evaluated before the arrival (guard 5 precedes the TRANSIT exit), so the arrival is **cancelled**: no E6, no body in the player's ship, no new mark; the record heads back to `from_body_id` (the home body with `RETURN_HOME` 1) after `RETURN_DELAY_TICKS`, and an ingress mark already laid stays (HE-20). No strike, no mark burst *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; the earlier text had the record arrive as LURK, which injected a CALM presence and marks into the ship that had just held its fire)*.
854	- **If a second TELL begins while the record is in RETREAT from the previous breach (E-HE-16)**: RETREAT → LURK → STALK on the new `tell_epoch`; it never skips LURK, and the per-epoch counters (`strikes_epoch`, `gouges_epoch`, `ruptures_epoch`, `chill_epoch_dj`, `chill_deposits_epoch`) reset at the first run that sees the new `tell_epoch` (lazy reset, transition guard 2), and `gouged_seg_ids` empties with them *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
855	- **If Attention's phase changes on a tick on which `horror.step` does not run (E-HE-17)**: Horror reads the view as committed by Attention's most recent run and acts at its next run, at most 4 ticks later (HE-4). A REACH can therefore begin up to 4 ticks after BREACH entry plus the approach; the delay only ever lengthens the warning.
856	- **If a seat is STAGGERED during a REACH (E-HE-18)**: the Controller freezes it and ignores input for `STAGGER_TICKS` 30 (PCI:170; STAGGERED is not the CRITICAL walk-only cap). A seat staggered at REACH start whose walk command is issued at tick 54 still clears at 90 (91 on a diagonal octant) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: HE-F5 tick-indexing convention, G4)*. A seat staggered mid-walk loses the frozen ticks plus a re-command, and clears only on draws long enough to absorb them. Horror does not adapt (no stored state). The stagger is itself Suit's or the Controller's told consequence (another axis reaching CRITICAL, or friendly harm). A strike-two stagger cannot overlap the next REACH because `STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS` 300 > `STAGGER_TICKS`.
857	
858	#### Degenerate strategies
859	
860	- **If a seat closes a door leaf between itself and the horror (E-HE-19)**: the leaf is solid to the horror (`solid_in`), it opens no door, and the straight segment from its foot point to P must not cross a closed leaf (HE-19), so no strike lands through it. Counterplay by design (HE-26); the price is the task and the ship under STRESS.
861	- **If the highest-`lux_pm` seat is in a room with no open route from the horror (E-HE-20)**: HE-13 still names that seat the target. The goal room is chosen over the full adjacency (closed leaves counted for distance), the movement uses the open-leaf graph, and the horror stops in the last reachable room at the closed leaf and begins no REACH (HE-14 condition (f) fails: `connected(horror foot, P)` is false across a closed leaf, and the distance test (d) alone would not stop it) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the earlier text cited a "segment test" that was not among conditions (a) to (e))*. It does not switch to a reachable but dimmer seat, because that would be a stored preference *(orchestrator ruling: HE-25 is silent on an unreachable target)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **It camps at the sill:** on the run it first becomes stationary there it lays one HAIRLINES mark on the leaf face (`held_at_leaf`, HE-26; no M17 call, no hull damage) and stays while that seat is the target and the phase is BREACH; the door is a visible, priced refuge, not a free one (delegated ruling G2, Open Question 33). A sealed seat is immune to the body; the Graph's own clocks and Attention's STRESS keep running. The share of told breaches with zero harm to a seat that stayed in the locus body is a playtest metric (30 to 60 % is the band; above 60 %, hull and ship consequences rise before any harm number does).
862	- **If the seat goes dark and stands still (E-HE-21)**: the target is the anchor on the next run (HE-13). The anchor REACH lays hairlines and, by default, one hull GOUGE under `GOUGES_PER_EPOCH_MAX` (HE-16 (3)); it never calls `apply_suit_damage` and never issues RUPTURE. Going dark spares the body and costs the ship, and every lit-only channelled verb is unavailable for the breach and the subside (about `BREACH_MIN_TICKS` + `SUBSIDE_TICKS` = 2100 ticks, 35 s). The anchor must lie within `HULL_CONTACT_PX` of a hull face for the GOUGE; if it does not, hairlines only.
863	- **If a dark seat stands within `R_SNAP_PX` of the anchor point at an anchor REACH's resolution (E-HE-22)**: no `apply_suit_damage` (an anchor REACH never harms a body, HE-16 (3)); the limb rests beside the seat and the hull takes the GOUGE. The seat has not been hunted, but a limb on its boots is not a safe place; whether a dark seat parked on the anchor should become targetable is an Open Question (the game-designer's `TOUCH_PX` guard was not adopted).
864	- **If the seat switches its lamp off after a REACH has begun (E-HE-23)**: P is already locked and stored; the strike resolves at P and hits every living seat in the disc, whether or not it was the target (HE-15). The lamp-off only changes the *next* run's target; nothing is remembered. Flapping the lamp to steer the horror costs the player the re-approach and cannot move a locked point.
865	- **If a seat stands in a thrown Chemlight pool (E-HE-24)**: the pool lights the seat, its `lux_pm` reaches `LIT_ON_PM` (a fresh Chemlight pool reads 700, so a seat standing in it is lit even with its own lamp off), and the seat is a candidate like any lit seat (HE-F8) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. The pool is never itself a target (a pool is not a seat). The glowstick works as a *work-light*: light the job, then step out of the pool dark; it does not pull the horror (HE-26).
866	- **If a seat walks through the horror (no collision) (E-HE-25)**: nothing happens in CALM, TELL or between REACHes; a rooted horror in REACH can be walked through, which may be an escape route out of a dead end. Accepted as a playtest item (Body's BDY-17: actors do not collide; the draw order decides how the overlap reads).
867	- **If a seat is in a dead-end room whose floor span is below `2 × R_SNAP_PX` (144 px) with a single exit (E-HE-26)**: it can be struck without a legal walk-out.
