872	#### Layout, weld and cut
873	
874	- **If a weld joins two bodies during a TELL or BREACH (E-HE-29)**: `locus_body` is the body in force at the call tick: recorded at TELL entry and replaced only by an AT-14 fallback (LOCUS_FALLBACK); a weld alone does not change it (AT-14); the horror's walkable graph does (recomputed on the `layout.state` change), so it may path across the new join. If the record's own section was in the absorbed body, its body-frame points (`pos_px`, `locked_pt`, `ingress_anchor_px`) are re-based by `frame_shift_px` on the next run and `body_id` becomes the survivor (HE-22, `offset_seen_px`) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. Strikes still require `exogenous_permitted(actor_section(seat))`, so a seat in a section outside `locus_body` is never hit.
875	- **If a cut removes the section the record stands in from its body (E-HE-30)**: `body_id` is re-derived from `body_of(section_id)` and the body-frame points are re-based by the new `section_offset(section_id) − offset_seen_px` (HE-22) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; if the section is gone the record goes TRANSIT with an egress mark and re-enters its home body by the HE-20 rule. Horror has no cut verb and never interrupts a cut (MSA-22) *(provisional — Modular Ship Assembly designed in this run)*.
876	- **If a Layout read returns NONE or UNKNOWN mid-path (E-HE-31)**: the record holds its last waypoint for at most `HOLD_MAX_RUNS` 12, then goes to LURK in CALM or TELL, stays in STALK holding position in BREACH, and goes to RETREAT in SUBSIDING (HE-25; never LURK in BREACH) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. UNKNOWN is never read as "unlit" or as "open" (HE-25). A REACH already in flight is not cancelled by a Layout change; the locked point is a stored integer.
877	- **If a door closes on the cached path (E-HE-32)**: the edge is excluded, the cache is recomputed once (`version(section_id)` of the section changed, C-HE-13 closed), and if the step reports no movement for `BLOCKED_RUNS_MAX` consecutive runs the cached hop is discarded and the path recomputed once more; a record still without movement after a second `BLOCKED_RUNS_MAX` runs is wedged and goes to RETREAT (HE-25) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
878	- **If no legal ingress entry exists (E-HE-33)**: the record stays in TRANSIT and retries every run; the diagnostic `horror_ingress_pending` is raised. A record still unregistered after the first Horror run at or after BREACH entry is a **cry-wolf defect** (the breach has no teeth; a record that registers on that run, at most 4 ticks after BREACH entry by run alignment, E-HE-17, is not) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, an acceptance criterion and an authoring signal, not a rule; the harm gates still require a registered record in the locus body, so nothing is struck. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **The rule relaxes before BREACH:** at `tell_enter_T + INGRESS_DELAY_TICKS + STALK_VISIBLE_FLOOR_TICKS` (540) the entry falls back to the nearest legal hull anchor (HE-F9) and the record registers at the first Horror run at or after 600 (exactly 600 when `tell_enter_T` mod 5 = 0, at most 604 otherwise) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, so the cry-wolf case is reachable only when every hull room of the locus body holds a living seat (AC-HE-44).
879	- **If the Layout chosen entry becomes illegal during the `INGRESS_MARK_LEAD_TICKS` window (a seat enters that room) (E-HE-34)**: the entry is re-chosen by the same rule; the first hairline mark stays (it is a true mark of where the web touched). The arrival is delayed to the new mark time plus the lead.
880	- **If a seat stands in an adjacent room within 72 px of P across a one-tile wall (E-HE-35)**: not hit. The disc is 1.5 tiles wide and wider than a wall, so the same-room test (HE-15) is the rule that stops a strike through a wall (Pillar 1: no lie about the world), and HE-14 condition (f) stops the REACH from *starting* when the horror stands on the far side of that wall, so no limb is drawn through it *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* A seat in the adjacent room across an **open, passable sill** is not hit either: the strike is strictly same-room (HE-15) even though a REACH could begin toward it (HE-19); AC-HE-27 carries the fixture.
881	- **If a leaf closes while the horror's foot box overlaps it (E-HE-57)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: Layout's close-safety counts seats' foot boxes, not the horror's, so the close succeeds; on the next run guard 4 ejects the horror along `−last_octant` in 8 px steps (at most 32 px, at most four `solid_in` queries) to the first free position (`horror_door_ejected`), or wedges it to RETREAT when none is free (`horror_wedged`); it is never embedded in the leaf (HE-26, AC-HE-137).
882	- **If a REACH is resolving while the layout changes under a linked seat (E-HE-58)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: `linked` (HE-19) flips once as a discrete event when a door opens or closes and never from a pixel-level move, so the standoff and step-away rules cannot oscillate at a doorway; the REACH already begun is untouched (the locked point is a stored integer).
883	
884	#### Save, restore and dormancy
885	
886	- **If a restore lands INTO REACH and `exogenous_permitted` still holds (E-HE-36)**: the record keeps its stored `locked_pt`, its `"horror.tell"` counter and its rooted state, and the remaining telegraph is exactly `reach_end_T − T_restore`: restore neither shortens nor lengthens it and never rerolls the draw. A save taken inside a REACH is Save/Load's SL-5 deferral case *(provisional — Save/Load: autosave is a soft gate that defers during a told breach)*, so the unfair case (a reload into the last ticks of a telegraph) is not Horror's to repair. Lengthening the telegraph on restore was considered (the game-designer's GF10 floor) and **rejected**: it mutates the simulation at restore time, breaks save-equivalence (G4) and SL-15's idempotent, no-clamp restore, and would make `snapshot(restore(snapshot()))` differ.
887	- **If a restore lands INTO REACH and the predicate no longer holds (the autosave predates a pod-hop or the breach ended) (E-HE-37)**: RETREAT with no strike, no hairlines and no GOUGE or RUPTURE (HE-41); the touch-down smear already in the ring stays.
888	- **If a restore lands INTO STRIKE (E-HE-38)**: the strike's `apply_suit_damage` and M17 calls were made on the entry run and are part of Suit's and the Graph's restored state; STRIKE is only the held snap pose and restoring it issues no second hit. `strike_T`, `seats_hit[]` and `strike_hull_seg` are persisted while the record is in STRIKE (HE-41), so the hit cue is not replayed *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
889	- **If a restore lands INTO TRANSIT with `transit_until_T` in the past (E-HE-39)**: legal; the record arrives at the next run with a legal entry. A TRANSIT record that also has a registered Emitter subject, or a non-TRANSIT record without a legal section, fails restore as `STATE_INCOHERENT`.
890	- **If any restored value is out of range (`strikes_epoch` above `STRIKES_EPOCH_MAX` 13, a mark ring longer than `MAX_MARKS`, a position outside its section, `acc_mpx` ≥ 1000) (E-HE-40)**: restore fails hard with the matching `HORROR_RESTORE_*` code (`RANGE`, `MARK_RING`, `SECTION_UNKNOWN`) and the Save/Load layer refuses the file; nothing is clamped (SL-15). A clamp would hide a corrupt save behind a plausible world.
891	- **If the player dies and the game restarts from the newest autosave (E-HE-41)**: `horror.state` restores with the WORLD blocks, including the `"horror.tell"` counter, exactly. The counter continues from its saved value, but the stream is re-keyed by the restore's `restore_epoch` through the kernel's `rng_derive_epoch` (HE-42, user ruling X8/D16, delegated ruling R1; *Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: kernel name*), so **the replay does not draw the same `UNFOLD_TICKS` sequence**: a death or loss of play is not a way to scout the telegraph lengths of the next breach, and (Save/Load's constraint) quit and death offer no reroll oracle (a Save & Quit then Continue of the newest `QUIT` generation carries the epoch and replays the same draws, so quitting cannot reroll; a death-stub restore advances it; delegated ruling R1 as amended by R13/R14) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R13/R14)*. The marks, positions and every physical fact are bit-identical to uninterrupted play given the pair (save, `restore_epoch`) (G4); the draws themselves stay inside the legal range, so the fairness bound of HE-F5 holds at every re-keyed draw; what the player learned stays in their head (Pillar 5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
892	- **If an autosave fires during CALM while a LURK stands at the standoff (E-HE-42)**: no Horror gate is needed; CALM is non-lethal by construction (HE-10), no lethal horror is ever adjacent to a seat in a CALM save, and SL-5 is unchanged. If the standoff rule is ever relaxed, SL-5 must be revisited.
893	- **If a record's body is unloaded (E-HE-43)**: the record is frozen, its marks do not age, its disturbances do not run and nothing fast-forwards on reload (HE-21, LS-17), **with one exception: a new `tell_epoch` whose locus body is not that body sends the record to TRANSIT at once (HE-20, guard 2), even though its own body is unloaded, with an egress mark laid in the unloaded section (inserted, not ageing)**. A record in TRANSIT whose destination unloads waits. If an unloaded record is somehow woken with a `last_seen_tell_epoch` that is two or more epochs old (a restored older save), the lazy reset zeroes its five epoch counters and empties `gouged_seg_ids` before any act, so its caps are never bound by a stale epoch *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
894	
895	#### Budgets, registration and determinism
896	
897	- **If `register_subject` (E6) returns false on a first registration (not a duplicate) (E-HE-44)**: the subject reads dark (`lux` 0, `lit` false); that is a **budget defect**, a failing criterion and a lint, never a gameplay state. The horror still moves and strikes (its harm does not depend on being a subject); the defect is that nothing can light it.
898	- **If a stub requests more footprints than the window allows (E-HE-45)**: at most `HE_FOOTPRINT_BUDGET` 8 per window are made, at most `MAX_DEPOSITS_PER_RUN` 4 per run; the rest are not attempted (a trace is a moment, not a queue) and counted `horror_footprints_withheld`. In nominal play the counter is 0; a nonzero count in a build is a defect.
899	- **If a mark insert mutates a packed array element without declaring its dirty key (E-HE-46)**: Godot 4.7 packed-array element writes do not call the setter, so the kernel would miss the change and `state_hash` would differ after a restore. Every mutation of the ring, the disturbance list and the record declares explicit dirty keys; a lint and a save-equivalence criterion enforce it.
900	- **If the same `world_seed`, the same (save, `restore_epoch`) pair and the same inputs are replayed (E-HE-47)**: the strike lengths, positions, marks, disturbance timings and `state_hash` are identical (HE-42). Randomness is `rng_derive` for the REACH length only; mark seeds, LURK waypoints and L3 timing are pure integer hashes of ids, the run index and `HE_HASH_SEED`.
901	
902	#### Hallucination and the Perception Filter
903	
904	- **If the Filter hides a real horror's body from one seat (Vertical Slice class (a), "hidden real entity") (E-HE-48)**: the marks, L3 state, M17 writes, `apply_suit_damage` calls and `horror.view` are bit-identical with and without the hide (HE-32). The limb tip and body are undrawn for that seat, but the touch-down smear at P is a true mark the Filter may not edit, so "a smear appeared under my feet" falsifies the hide at a cost of looking at the floor. The hide collapses when `horror.view` reports a state outside {LURK, RETREAT} *(provisional — Sanity & Hallucination Rules designed in this run)*.
905	- **If a phantom horror co-occurs with a real one (E-HE-49)**: the phantom has no record, no mark, no footprint, no registration and no strike (HE-32); the real one proceeds on its own clock. A seat that flees the phantom can walk into the real disc; "is the floor marked?" is the check, and TellAudit records nothing for the phantom (AT E-53).
906	- **If the Filter shows a crewmate as a horror and a seat harms that crewmate (Vertical Slice class (c)) (E-HE-50)**: that is the friendly-harm act under Interaction and Sanity's gate, not Horror's; no Horror state changes. The rig presenter is only the substitute body; a real horror emits nothing and carries no beam, so the true beam remains a perfect discriminator (HE-2).
907	- **If a seat's own Sanity state makes it see violet fringes or false gauges (E-HE-51)**: Horror's marks, disturbances and positions are TRUTH channel and are not corruptible; the body can be omitted or wholly substituted only by the Filter, and marks never use flesh or violet (HE-31). Horror reads no `PERCEPTION_OUT` block (CR-12).
908	
909	#### Co-op hooks (Vertical Slice and later)
910	
911	- **If two lit seats are in the locus body (E-HE-52)**: the higher `lux_pm` wins; a tie goes to the lower seat id; a stateless argmax can alternate as lamps change, and a hysteresis would need a stored value (C-HE-19, an Open Question). A strike hits every living seat in the disc once, in ascending player id, each as its own `apply_suit_damage` call.
912	- **If a seat is DOWNED by a teammate (friendly harm) or by another cause during a REACH (E-HE-53)**: it is not "living, non-DOWNED" at resolution and is not hit; the REACH completes harmlessly and the record RETREATs. DOWNED and DEAD seats are never candidates (HE-18).
913	- **If a second record is requested while `HORROR_MAX_MVP` is 1 (E-HE-54)**: the request is refused by the data lint and the boot check; at runtime `S_h ≤ HORROR_SUBJECTS_MAX` 2 is a ceiling reserved for the transient during ingress. Rosters per ring and more types are Vertical Slice.
914	- **If a seat is in a different body from `locus_body` (E-HE-55)**: it is not a candidate in TELL, BREACH or SUBSIDING, is never hit, and is not the subject of the predicate (the predicate's argument is Body's `actor_section`, not the Graph's `section_of`). In CALM the candidates are the seats in the record's own body.

content.content:
951	## Tuning Knobs
952	
953	Every Horror-owned value lives in the per-type data file keyed by `type_id` (HE-5, R26); no behavioural constant lives in code. Every default is a **`[PLACEHOLDER]`** pending playtest, and every row is a candidate for the registry, written from this final text by a later stage. **★ marks a value that a neighbour quotes or that a registered relation binds** (a cross-system fact: another GDD, the registry or an acceptance criterion outside this document reads it); an unstarred knob is Horror-internal. Durations are authored as integer counts of runs (`HORROR_RUN_TICKS` 5) and published in ticks; a duration that is not a multiple of 5 is a data-load failure (HE-4, E-HE-4). "Interacts with" names the formula or neighbour that binds the row; the formula, not the row, is the source of truth for any two-bound.
954	
955	**The dials that move lethality are not in this table.** `STRIKE_BP` cannot change the hits-to-FAILED count inside its registered interval (HE-F3), so "make it more lethal" is a request to change the per-attempt miss rate `p`, the attempts per breach, the breaches per session (Attention's) or repair availability (Suit's). The first of these is telegraph legibility (HE-14 and the blind-legibility criteria), not a number.
956	
957	#### Speeds and ranges
958

**Example:** A weld dirties 14 Graph keys → delivered as 14 keys; a hull breach cascading through 300 nodes → `ALL`; Failure & Trail does one full re-read.

**D.10 RNG stream derivation**

The `rng_derive` formula is defined as: *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: GDScript `int` is signed 64-bit and `>>` is an arithmetic shift, so every shift is a masked logical shift and every constant is written signed)*

`rng_derive(world_seed, stream_name, counter) = mix64( world_seed ⊕ mix64(fnv64(stream_name)) ⊕ (counter × GOLDEN) )`; `unit = lsr(rng_derive, 11) / 2^53`; `rng_int(lo, hi) = lo + floor(unit × (hi − lo + 1))`

with `lsr(x, n) = (x >> n) & ((1 << (64 − n)) − 1)` for 1 ≤ n ≤ 63 (logical shift); `mix64(z)` = the SplitMix64 finaliser: `z = (z ⊕ lsr(z, 30)) × C1; z = (z ⊕ lsr(z, 27)) × C2; return z ⊕ lsr(z, 31)`; `fnv64` = FNV-1a over the UTF-8 bytes of the name, `h = FNV_OFFSET; for each byte: h = (h ⊕ byte) × FNV_PRIME`, **computed once per stream at registration and cached, never per draw**.
